1.1: This the vision Isaiah, son of Amoz, saw—bout Judah and Jerusalem—while Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah was king.
1.2: "Listen up, heavens! Pay attention, earth! God talkin': I raised these kids up right, and they still turned they back on Me."
1.3: "Even the ox know who feedin' it. The donkey know where home at. But My people? Israel act like they got no clue who I am."
1.4: "Man, y'all a whole sinful nation. Just heavy with mess. Y'all full of wrongdoers—corrupt kids who wildin' out. Y'all done dipped on the Lord and disrespected the Holy One of Israel. Straight up turned your backs."
1.5: "Why keep gettin' beat down? Y'all just gon' keep wildin'? From the head to the toe, y'all sick. Brain foggy, heart weak."
1.6: "Ain't nothin' healthy left—just wounds, bruises, and open sores. Ain't nobody tryna clean it, bandage it up, or even show care."
1.7: "Your land? Wasted. Cities? Burnt down. Strangers eatin' off your plate right in your face. Everything lookin' like a war zone."
1.8: "Zion, My daughter, sittin' like a little shack in a vineyard, like a lonely hut in a cucumber field, like a city under siege."
1.9: "If the Lord of hosts ain't left a small remnant, we'd be out here like Sodom and Gomorrah—done for."
1.10: "Listen to the Word of the Lord, you 'leaders of Sodom.' Pay attention, folks of Gomorrah. This for y'all."
1.11: "All them sacrifices y'all bringin'? I ain't impressed," says the Lord. "I don't need no more burnt rams or fatty calves. That blood from bulls, lambs, goats? Miss Me with it."
1.12: "Y'all keep showin' up in My house, but who told you to come stomp through My courts like that?"
1.13: "Stop bringin' Me these empty gifts. That incense? Stinks. Your new moons, Sabbaths, church events—I ain't messin' with none of it when y'all still livin' foul."
1.14: "Your celebrations? I hate 'em. They drain Me. I'm tired of watchin' y'all fake it."
1.15: "Y'all throw your hands up to pray? I'm turnin' My eyes. Pray all you want—I ain't hearin' you. Y'all hands got blood on 'em."
1.16: "Wash up. Get clean. Drop all that evil in front of Me. Cut it out."
1.17: "Learn how to do right. Go after justice. Check the oppressor. Speak up for orphans. Fight for the widows."
1.18: "Come here, let's talk it out," says the Lord. "Y'all sins look red like blood? I can make 'em white like snow. Crimson red? I'll make it white like wool."
1.19: "If y'all down to listen and obey, you'll eat good in this land."
1.20: "But if y'all act hard-headed and rebel? That sword comin' for you. And that's on God—I said what I said."
1.21: "Look at this city that used to be faithful. Now it's out here actin' like a prostitute. Used to be full of justice, but now? Just killers."
1.22: "Your silver? Trash now. Your wine? Watered down."
1.23: "Your leaders? Rebels hangin' with thieves. All they want is a bribe. They chasin' clout. They don't care about orphans. Widows ain't even on they radar."
1.24: "So the Lord, the Lord of hosts, Israel's Mighty One, say this: 'Bet. I'ma handle My enemies. Time to clean house.'"
1.25: "I'ma pull up on y'all Myself. Burn away all the fake. Scrub you down from top to bottom."
1.26: "I'ma bring back real judges, like we used to have. Real counselors. Then they gon' call you the Righteous City again—the Faithful Spot."
1.27: "Zion gon' get saved through justice. The folks who turn back? Righteousness got them covered."
1.28: "But folks still wildin'? Them transgressors and sinners? They all gettin' taken out. Ain't no salvation for the ones that ditch the Lord."
1.29: "Y'all gon' be ashamed of them sacred trees y'all was chasin' after. Embarrassed of them wild gardens y'all was feelin'."
1.30: "Y'all gon' be like a dead tree in autumn. A dried-up garden with no water."
1.31: "The strong folks? Like dry kindling. All their work? Just sparks. When they catch fire together, ain't nobody comin' to put it out."

2.1: This that word Isaiah, son of Amoz, saw about Judah and Jerusalem.
2.2: In the last days, God's house gon' be sittin' high—higher than every mountain, lifted above all the hills. And folks from everywhere? They gon' be runnin' to it.
2.3: Whole crowds gon' be sayin', "Let's roll up to God's mountain, to the house of Jacob's God. He gon' teach us how to live right, and we gon' walk that path." 'Cause the law? It's comin' outta Zion. And the Word of the Lord? Straight from Jerusalem.
2.4: He gon' be the Judge over all nations. He gon' call folks out. And guess what? They gon' turn they swords into plows and their spears into garden tools. Ain't nobody gon' be fightin' no more. Ain't even gon' study war no more.
2.5: Come on, people of Jacob—let's walk in God's light, not in the dark.
2.6: But Lord, You turned from Your people, the house of Jacob, 'cause they out here doin' East side rituals, talkin' like Philistine psychics, and mixin' with folks who don't know You.
2.7: They land flooded with silver and gold—money for days. Got horses and chariots too, stacked up with no end.
2.8: They also got idols on idols—worshippin' what they made with they own hands, like they own lil' gods.
2.9: Folks bowin' low to these man-made things, humblin' theyself before nonsense. Don't forgive 'em, Lord—they know better.
2.10: Run and hide in the rocks, lay low in the dirt—'cause when God shows up in power, folks gon' be terrified. His glory too much to handle.
2.11: All that pride? Gon' get knocked down. All that big ego? Humbled. On that day, only the Lord gon' be lifted up.
2.12: The Lord of hosts got a day marked for every prideful, puffed-up thing. If it's lifted, He bringin' it low.
2.13: From the tall cedars in Lebanon to the mighty oaks in Bashan—if it standin' tall, He choppin' it down.
2.14: All them high mountains and lifted hills? They comin' down too.
2.15: Every tall tower, every wall folks think make 'em safe? Gone.
2.16: Every ship from Tarshish, every fancy boat and sleek vessel? He clearin' it out.
2.17: Man's pride gettin' dropped. Arrogance? Canceled. That day only got one spotlight—God's.
2.18: All them idols? He trashin' every last one.
2.19: Folks gon' run into caves and hide in holes in the ground, tryin' to escape the terror of the Lord and the weight of His glory when He steps in and shakes the whole earth.
2.20: On that day, folks gon' throw out their gold and silver idols—tossin' 'em to moles and bats. That's how worthless they'll look.
2.21: They gon' duck into rocky cliffs and craggy cracks, tryna hide from the Lord's presence when He rise up and rock the earth for real.
2.22: So cut ties with these folks who think they all that—just humans with breath in they nose. Why they got y'all pressed anyway?

3.1: Look, the Lord—yeah, the Lord of Heaven's Armies—He takin' back everything from Judah and Jerusalem: no more food in the pantry, no water in the jug.
3.2: All the strong men gone. Soldiers? Outta here. Judges, prophets, fortune-tellers, elders? All of 'em snatched.
3.3: No captains, no respected OGs, no counselors, no skilled builders, no magic men. It's a full wipeout.
3.4: "I'ma let these little kids run things—babies gon' be actin' like they in charge."
3.5: Folks gon' be out here oppressin' each other—every man for himself. Kids talkin' reckless to grown folks, low-lifes dissin' the ones who earned respect.
3.6: One brother gon' grab another like, "Yo, you got a decent fit on—go ahead and lead us. This place a mess, but you can fix it, right?"
3.7: But the dude gon' be like, "Man, I ain't got no solutions. My crib broke too—no food, no fits. Don't look at me to run nothin'."
3.8: Jerusalem trippin', Judah already face-planted—'cause they mouthin' off and livin' straight against the Lord. They wildin' in God's face like He don't see.
3.9: You can see the guilt all on they faces. They not even ashamed—flexin' sin like it's a badge. Just like Sodom. Woe to them—they brought this mess on theyselves.
3.10: Tell the righteous folks: they gon' be alright. They gon' eat the fruit of the good they planted.
3.11: But the wicked? It's gon' be all bad. What they put out, they 'bout to get back.
3.12: My people got kids bossin' them around, and women runnin' the show. The ones leadin' y'all? They drivin' y'all straight into a ditch.
3.13: But the Lord steppin' up now. He about to make His case and lay down judgment.
3.14: The Lord 'bout to call out the elders and leaders, like, "Y'all out here eatin' up My vineyard! You got stolen goods from the poor stashed in your houses."
3.15: "Why y'all crushin' My people? Why you grindin' the faces of the poor into the dirt?" That's from the Lord, the God of Angel Armies.
3.16: Then the Lord said: "These daughters of Zion out here actin' all high and mighty—chin up, eyes flirtin', switchin' down the block with bells on they ankles like they runway ready."
3.17: "So I'ma hit the top of they heads with a scab, and expose what they think they hidin'."
3.18: "That day, I'm takin' all the extra off 'em: them jinglin' anklets, them scarves, them moon-shaped bling."
3.20: "Headwraps, ankle chains, fancy belts, perfume boxes, charms? Gone."
3.22: "Designer fits, capes, and purses? Say goodbye."
3.23: "All them mirrors, silk linens, turbans, and robes? Gone with the wind."
3.24: "Instead of smellin' sweet, y'all gon' stink. Instead of luxury belts, ropes. Instead of fresh hair, bald heads. Instead of fine robes, burlap. Instead of beauty, brands like cattle."
3.25: "Y'all men gon' die in war, and the strong ones gon' drop by the sword."
3.26: "The city gates gon' cry out. And the women left behind? Gonna be sittin' on the ground, empty, broken, and alone."

4.1: In that day, seven women gon' run up on one man like, "We ain't askin' for your money or your name—just let us claim you so we don't walk around ashamed and single out here."
4.2: But hold up—on that same day, the branch of the Lord gon' shine bright and beautiful. What He grows in the land gon' be full of pride and joy for the ones still standin' in Israel.
4.3: Anybody still breathin' in Zion, anybody still holdin' it down in Jerusalem? They gon' be called holy—names written in the book of life like, "Yeah, they made it."
4.4: When the Lord finally scrubs all that dirt off the daughters of Zion, when He rinses out the bloodstains from Jerusalem, He gon' do it with a spirit of justice and a fire that cleans everything up.
4.5: Then God gon' set it off—cover every house on Mount Zion with a cloud and smoke in the daytime, and light it up with a pillar of fire at night. His glory gon' sit like a divine canopy over it all.
4.6: And under that glory? You gon' have shade from the heat, shelter from storms, and a whole safe space when the rain starts fallin'.

5.1: Lemme sing a lil somethin' for my Beloved—about His vineyard, a song from the heart: My Beloved had a vineyard, planted on a good, fertile hill.
5.2: He put in work—dug it up, cleared the stones, planted top-tier vines. Built a tower in it too, and a winepress ready to go. He was expectin' sweet grapes… but it gave Him wild, bitter ones.
5.3: "So now, people of Jerusalem and Judah, y'all judge this with Me: Me vs. My vineyard."
5.4: "What more could I have done for My vineyard? I did everything. So why, when I expected good fruit, did I get this wild mess?"
5.5: "Lemme tell y'all what I'm 'bout to do: I'm takin' down the fence—it's gon' get trampled. I'm removin' the protection—it's gon' burn."
5.6: "I'm lettin' it go to waste. No more pruning, no more care. Thorns and weeds gon' take over. I'm even tellin' the clouds—don't rain on it no more."
5.7: This vineyard? That's Israel. The folks of Judah? That was His favorite planting. He looked for justice—got bloodshed. He looked for righteousness—heard cries for help instead.
5.8: Woe to the folks buyin' up house after house, field after field—till nobody got room left. Y'all buildin' like you own the whole land.
5.9: I heard the Lord say it straight: "These big, pretty houses? Empty. No one livin' in 'em."
5.10: "Ten acres of vineyard gon' barely give you one bucket of juice. You plant a whole load of seed and get back crumbs."
5.11: Woe to the ones up early just to chase liquor, and stay lit all night off wine.
5.12: Harps, strings, tambourines, flutes, and drinks at every party—but they ignore God's work and don't even peep what He's doin' behind the scenes.
5.13: That's why My people in bondage—no knowledge. The ones who were supposed to be honorable? Starvin'. The crowd? Thirsty and dry.
5.14: So Sheol (the grave) just stretched its mouth wide. The proud, the partiers, the showy ones—all gon' get swallowed up.
5.15: Folks gon' be humbled, brought low, real quick. All them proud eyes? Dropped down.
5.16: But the Lord of Heaven's Armies gon' be lifted up in justice. The Holy God gon' be honored in righteousness.
5.17: Then lambs gon' graze like it's nothin', and strangers gon' eat in the ruins of the rich.
5.18: Woe to them who drag sin around like it's nothin'—pullin' it behind 'em like a cart full of lies.
5.19: They be sayin', "Tell God to hurry up and show us somethin'. Let Him prove Himself if He real."
5.20: Woe to the ones callin' evil good and good evil—flippin' light into darkness and sweet into bitter. Y'all got it backwards.
5.21: Woe to the folks who think they so smart, wise in their own minds.
5.22: Woe to them drink champs—mighty when it come to wine, skilled at mixin' strong drinks,
5.23: Who let the wicked off the hook for a bribe, and take justice away from the innocent.
5.24: That's why, like dry grass catchin' fire, they gon' burn. Their roots rotten, flowers turn to dust—'cause they rejected the Word of the Lord and threw shade at the Holy One of Israel.
5.25: So God mad now—for real. He done raised His hand and struck 'em down. Mountains shook. Bodies layin' in the streets like trash. And even with all that? God still not done. His hand still up.
5.26: He gon' raise a banner to signal nations from far away—callin' 'em with a whistle. And they gon' come fast, no delay.
5.27: They ain't tired, they ain't stumbling. Ain't nobody sleepin'. Belts tight, sandals strong.
5.28: Their arrows sharp, bows pulled back. Their horses movin' like fire on pavement. Wheels spinnin' like storms.
5.29: They gon' roar like lions, snatch up prey, and nobody gon' be able to stop 'em.
5.30: That day, the roar gon' sound like the sea. You look out at the land? Just darkness and pain. Even the light? Covered up by storm clouds.

6.1: The year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord—seated high up on His throne, lifted above it all. His robe was so long, it filled the whole temple.
6.2: Above Him were these heavenly beings called seraphim—each one had six wings. Two wings covered their face, two covered their feet, and with the other two, they flew.
6.3: And they was callin' back and forth: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Heaven's Armies! The whole earth full of His glory!"
6.4: As they shouted, the doorposts shook, and the whole temple filled up with smoke.
6.5: I said, "Oh no—it's over for me. I'm messed up! My mouth ain't clean, and I live around people whose mouths dirty too. And now I done seen the King—the Lord of hosts—with my own eyes!"
6.6: Then one of the seraphim flew over to me, holdin' a hot coal with tongs, straight from the altar.
6.7: He touched my mouth with it and said, "Look, this coal touched your lips—your guilt gone, your sins cleaned up."
6.8: Then I heard God's voice: "Who should I send? Who gon' go out for Us?" And I said, "I'm right here—send me!"
6.9: He said, "Aight. Go tell these people: 'Keep listenin'… but you still won't get it. Keep lookin'… but y'all still blind.'"
6.10: "Make they hearts heavy, ears plugged, eyes shut. So they don't see, don't hear, don't understand—not with their heart, not with their soul. 'Cause if they really did, they'd turn back and I'd heal 'em."
6.11: Then I said, "Lord… how long I gotta do this?" And He said, "Until all the cities empty, The houses vacant, And the whole land ruined.
6.12: The Lord gon' send people far out, And the land gon' be full of abandoned places."
6.13: "But even then… a tenth will remain. And even they gon' get hit again. Like when a terebinth or oak tree gets chopped down— But the stump still stands. That stump? That's the holy seed."

7.1: Back when Ahaz (son of Jotham, son of Uzziah) was king of Judah, Rezin (king of Syria) and Pekah (son of Remaliah, king of Israel) pulled up to make war on Jerusalem—but they couldn't break through.
7.2: Word got back to the royal fam: "Syria linking up with Ephraim!" That news shook Ahaz and the whole crew—they were shook like trees in the wind.
7.3: Then the Lord told Isaiah, "Take your boy Shear-Jashub and go meet Ahaz by the water system near the upper pool, by the road to the laundry spot.
7.4: Tell him this: 'Stay calm. Chill. Don't trip, don't panic. Them two clowns—Rezin and Remaliah's boy? They just burnt-out fire sticks.
7.5: Yeah, they plannin' evil against you—Syria, Ephraim, and that other dude talkin' bout,
7.6: "Let's invade Judah, shake things up, and crown some random dude, Tabel's son, to rule it."'
7.7: But the Lord God says, "Nah. That ain't gon' happen. That plot won't stick."
7.8: "Syria's capital is Damascus, and Rezin runnin' that. Ephraim? In 65 years, they gon' be done—no more people, no more power.
7.9: Samaria's the head of Ephraim, and Remaliah's son runnin' that. But if you don't believe what I say, Ahaz, you ain't gon' stand firm. Period."
7.10: Then the Lord told Ahaz again,
7.11: "Go 'head, ask Me for a sign—deep as the grave or high up in the sky. Whatever you want."
7.12: But Ahaz was like, "Nah, I ain't tryna test God like that."
7.13: Isaiah clapped back, "Y'all House of David really out here wearin' people out—and now you gon' try God too?
7.14: Bet. The Lord Himself gon' give y'all a sign anyway: Look, a virgin gon' get pregnant and have a Son. His name? Immanuel—'God with us.'
7.15: He gon' eat curds and honey, and He'll know how to say no to wrong and yes to good.
7.16: But before He old enough to make choices, both those kings you scared of? Their land gon' be empty."
7.17: "But hear this too—God bringin' the king of Assyria down on y'all, your people, and your whole fam. Ain't been times this rough since Israel split from Judah."
7.18: That day, the Lord gon' whistle for flies from Egypt and bees from Assyria—and they all comin'.
7.19: They gon' settle in valleys, cracks in rocks, thorn bushes, and fields.
7.20: And on that same day, God gon' shave y'all clean—head, legs, even the beard—using Assyria like a hired razor.
7.21: Back then, folks gon' be so broke, one man just keep a young cow and two sheep alive.
7.22: And that little bit of milk they produce? That's gon' be survival food. Everybody left eatin' curds and honey.
7.23: Places that used to have vineyards worth stacks? Overrun with thorns and weeds now.
7.24: Folks gon' walk in with bows and arrows—'cause the whole land look like a wilderness now.
7.25: Even the good farmland too dangerous to farm—covered in briars. So it'll just be a space for oxen and sheep to roam.

8.1: Then the Lord told me, "Grab a big scroll and write this loud and clear: Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz."
8.2: He said, "I'm bringin' in two solid witnesses—Uriah the priest and Zechariah, Jeberechiah's son—to make it official."
8.3: So I went to my wife, the prophetess, and she got pregnant and had a son. Then God said, "Name him Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz (Quick to plunder, swift to spoil).
8.4: Before that boy even learns how to say 'Mama' or 'Dada,' Damascus and Samaria's riches gon' be snatched up by the king of Assyria."
8.5: Then God spoke to me again and said:
8.6: "Since these folks rejected the gentle waters of Shiloah, and instead celebrated Rezin and Remaliah's son,
8.7: I'm bringin' in the big flood—Assyria and all its pride. That river gon' rise, overflow its banks…
8.8: …and flood through Judah. It's gon' rise so high, it'll come up to your neck. The wings of that empire gon' spread across your whole land, O Immanuel."
8.9: "Y'all better brace yourselves, nations. Y'all gon' break. Go ahead and suit up—still gon' break. Go ahead and plan—still won't work. Speak on it if you want—but it won't stand. Why? 'Cause God is with us."
8.10: Plot all you want. It won't land.
8.11: The Lord pressed this on me heavy, sayin': "Don't live how they live. Don't follow their ways."
8.12: "Stop callin' everything a conspiracy just 'cause the crowd do. Don't be spooked like they are.
8.13: Fear Me. Respect Me. That's the only fear you need."
8.14: "I'll be a safe place to some… but to others? I'll trip 'em up. I'll be a rock that offends both Israel and Judah. A trap for the ones in Jerusalem."
8.15: "They gon' stumble, fall, and break. Get caught up and captured."
8.16: Lock this prophecy down. Pass the message on to My people.
8.17: I'ma wait on the Lord—even if He hidin' His face from Jacob right now. I'm still puttin' my hope in Him.
8.18: Look, it's me and the kids the Lord gave me—we're walkin' billboards for signs and wonders in Israel. From the Lord of Heaven's Armies, who lives up on Mount Zion.
8.19: And when folks start tellin' you, "Go talk to mediums and fortune-tellers—listen to the whispers and mumbles," don't fall for that. Ain't y'all supposed to be seekin' God? Why y'all askin' the dead for advice on life?
8.20: Go back to the law. Go back to the truth. If they ain't speakin' God's word, it's 'cause they walkin' in darkness. Ain't no light in 'em.
8.21: They gon' wander around stressed and hungry. And when the hunger hits hard, they gon' get mad—curse they king and even curse God, lookin' up like, "Why this happenin'?"
8.22: Then they'll look down and all they'll see is despair—darkness, sorrow, anguish. No light in sight. Just deep, deep darkness.

9.1: But hold up—the darkness ain't forever. That gloom over Galilee? It won't last. Yeah, God humbled Zebulun and Naphtali for a minute, but He 'bout to bless that same region by the sea, across the Jordan, in the land of outsiders.
9.2: The people walkin' in the dark? They done seen a big, bold light. Folks sittin' in the shadow of death? That light just hit 'em.
9.3: You grew the nation, God, and the joy exploded! They celebratin' like it's harvest season or like they just split the bag after a big win.
9.4: You broke their chains—snapped the yoke off their necks, crushed the oppressor's rod, just like You did back when You showed out in Midian.
9.5: Every boot from the battlefield, every bloody uniform, gon' get tossed in the fire—burned for good.
9.6: 'Cause a Child been born to us. A Son got given. He carryin' the whole government on His back. And His name gon' be: Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
9.7: His rule and His peace? No limits. He takin' the throne of David and holdin' it down forever—with real justice and judgment. This ain't temporary. And God's passion? That's what's makin' it happen.
9.8: The Lord sent a word to Jacob—and boom, it landed right on Israel.
9.9: Everybody gon' know—Ephraim and all the folks in Samaria—that pride talk they been runnin':
9.10: "Yeah, the bricks fell, but we comin' back stronger. We usin' cut stone now. The trees got knocked down? Cool—we plantin' cedars next."
9.11: So God said, "Bet." He stirred up Rezin's enemies against him—He turnin' the heat up.
9.12: Syrians attack from the front, Philistines from the back. Israel gettin' chewed up with no mercy. But even after all this? God's anger ain't cooled off. His hand still stretched out.
9.13: And the people still ain't turnin' to God, the One who strikin' 'em. They not even seekin' Him.
9.14: So He cuttin' off the head and the tail—top to bottom—in one day.
9.15: The head? That's the elders and big shots. The tail? That's them fake prophets spreadin' lies.
9.16: These so-called leaders leadin' folks off a cliff. And everybody followin' 'em? Headed for destruction.
9.17: That's why God ain't showin' no joy in their young men. Ain't feelin' no mercy for the fatherless or the widows—'cause everybody out here wildin'. Hypocrites, evildoers, talkin' nonsense. But even with that? His anger still burnin'. His hand still stretched out.
9.18: Wickedness out here blazin' like wildfire—burnin' through bushes, forests, everything in sight. The smoke risin' up heavy.
9.19: God's wrath settin' the whole land on fire. People turnin' into fuel. Ain't nobody showin' love—not even to they own kin.
9.20: They reachin' to the right—still hungry. Munchin' to the left—still empty. It's so bad, folks gon' be eatin' the flesh of their own arms.
9.21: Manasseh goin' at Ephraim. Ephraim goin' at Manasseh. And both together gunnin' for Judah. But through all this mess? God's anger ain't turned away—His hand still stretched out.

10.1: Woe to the ones writin' up crooked laws—legal traps just to keep the poor down.
10.2: They robbin' folks of justice, takin' from the broke, preyin' on widows, snatchin' from orphans like it's a game.
10.3: What y'all gon' do when judgment day hits? When destruction shows up from way out? Who you gon' run to for help? Where's all that clout gon' go?
10.4: Without Me, you gon' be layin' with the prisoners—or fallin' with the dead. But even still… God's anger ain't turned away. His hand still stretched out.
10.5: Woe to Assyria, that stick I been usin' to swing My anger—the rod in My hand bringin' heat.
10.6: I sent him to go check a godless nation, to take what's theirs, crush 'em like dirt in the streets.
10.7: But he wasn't even thinkin' 'bout Me—he just wanted to wreck nations, take over like a boss.
10.8: "Aren't all my officers like kings?" he brags.
10.9: "Didn't I handle Calno like Carchemish? Hamath like Arpad? Samaria just like Damascus?"
10.10: "I conquered nations full of idols, even worse than Jerusalem or Samaria!"
10.11: "If I crushed Samaria and her idols, Jerusalem next—easy work."
10.12: But once God done using Assyria to clean house in Zion, He gon' turn around and deal with Assyria's arrogant heart and prideful face.
10.13: 'Cause Assyria been sayin': "I did this with my own strength, my own smarts. I moved borders, stole riches, crushed cities like a real one."
10.14: "I snatched wealth like bird eggs—nobody said nothin'. Not even a flap or chirp."
10.15: But hold up—does the axe brag over the one swingin' it? The saw boast over the one holdin' it? That stick just a stick, it ain't movin' on its own.
10.16: So God 'bout to humble Assyria's big shots—make 'em skinny, take the shine off, and light a fire under their pride.
10.17: Israel's God gon' be that flame—burnin' up all their mess in one day.
10.18: That fire gon' eat their fancy forests and crops—burnin' soul and body. They gon' fade like a sick man wastin' away.
10.19: What's left of their army? So few, a kid could count 'em.
10.20: On that day, the ones left in Israel—the survivors from Jacob's crew—they ain't gon' lean on their enemy no more. They gon' lean on the Lord for real this time.
10.21: The remnant comin' back home—to the Mighty God.
10.22: Israel might be as many as the sand of the sea, but only a remnant comin' back. Judgment is comin' in waves—but it'll be soaked in righteousness.
10.23: God not playin'. He gon' bring it to a close—quick, complete, and just—in the whole land.
10.24: So God says: "My people in Zion, don't be scared of Assyria. Yeah, they swingin' a rod at you like Egypt did,
10.25: but it's just for a moment. My anger gon' pass, and then I'ma handle them."
10.26: Just like I crushed Midian at Oreb, or split the sea in Egypt—I'ma do it again.
10.27: That day, the burden gon' lift off your shoulders. The yoke around your neck? Snapped. Because of the anointing.
10.28: Look, they marchin'—already at Aiath, passin' through Migron, settin' up at Michmash.
10.29: Comin' down the ridge, posted up in Geba. Ramah shakin', Gibeah gone ghost.
10.30: Gallim cryin' loud. Laish can hear it. Anathoth stressed out.
10.31: Madmenah on the run. Folks in Gebim hidin' out.
10.32: By the time they reach Nob, they gon' be shakin' fists at Jerusalem like they runnin' the block.
10.33: But the Lord—yeah, the Lord of Hosts—He steppin' in to chop down the tall ones. All that pride? Gettin' axed.
10.34: He slicin' through forests like a lumberjack. Even mighty Lebanon? Fallin' before the Mighty One.

11.1: Outta Jesse's family tree, a new branch gon' rise up. Fresh growth from old roots—He the One.
11.2: God's Spirit gon' rest on Him. He walkin' in full power: Spirit of wisdom, Spirit of understanding, Spirit of guidance and strength, Spirit of knowledge and deep reverence for the Lord.
11.3: He love the fear of the Lord—ain't moved by what He sees or hears. He don't judge on looks or gossip.
11.4: He gon' ride for the poor with full righteousness. He gon' bring justice for the meek—fair and solid. He gon' speak truth so hard, it shake the earth. His breath? That's enough to shut wicked folks down.
11.5: Righteousness gon' be wrapped around His waist like a belt. Faithfulness? Tied to Him like a sash.
11.6: Wolves gon' chill with lambs. Leopards nappin' with goats. Calves, lions, and baby cows out here hangin'—and a little child leadin' the crew.
11.7: Cows and bears out here grazin' together, their babies layin' side by side. Lions eatin' straw like oxen—no more bloodshed.
11.8: Babies playin' near cobra dens. Toddlers reachin' into snake holes—no fear.
11.9: Ain't nobody hurtin' nobody on God's holy mountain. Why? 'Cause the whole earth gon' be soaked in the knowledge of God like water over the sea.
11.10: On that day, the Root of Jesse gon' stand tall—like a banner to the nations. Even the Gentiles gon' look to Him. His presence? Glorious.
11.11: And when that day hits, God gon' reach out again—second time—pullin' back the remnant of His people from everywhere: Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath—even from the islands out in the sea.
11.12: He liftin' that banner again—callin' the scattered ones home. He bringin' the outcasts of Israel, and Judah's exiles, from the four corners of the globe.
11.13: All that beef between Ephraim and Judah? Done. No more jealousy, no more drama.
11.14: They gon' ride together—fly down on the Philistines, take back what's theirs from the east, and put hands on Edom and Moab. Even Ammon gon' fall in line.
11.15: God gon' dry up that sea tongue in Egypt—strike the river with His wind, break it into seven paths so folks can cross dry like it's Exodus 2.0.
11.16: A whole highway gon' open for the remnant from Assyria—just like when He brought Israel up outta Egypt the first time.

12.1: On that day, you gon' say: "Lord, I gotta praise You. Yeah, You was mad at me, But now You done pulled that anger back, and gave me comfort instead."
12.2: "Look, God is my salvation. I ain't scared no more—I trust Him. 'Cause Yah, the Lord, is my strength and my song. He done became my whole salvation."
12.3: So with pure joy, we out here drawin' up water from the deep wells of salvation—overflowin'.
12.4: That day, folks gon' be shoutin': "Give God His praise! Call on His name! Tell the world what He did—don't keep it to yourself! Let everybody know His name is high and lifted!"
12.5: "Sing to the Lord! He been doin' great things! And the whole earth know about it."
12.6: "Turn the volume up, Zion! Cry out and shout! 'Cause the Holy One of Israel? He right there, livin' in the middle of y'all!"

13.1: This the heavy word Isaiah, son of Amoz, got about Babylon.
13.2: "Put up the banner on a high hill. Shout it loud. Wave your hand so the troops know it's go time—let 'em march straight into the fancy gates.
13.3: I done summoned My chosen ones, My real ones—powerful folk who ride for Me, and who ain't afraid of My fire. They gon' handle business."
13.4: Listen—it's loud out in them mountains. Nations gathered. Armies mobbin'. God pullin' His whole squad together for battle.
13.5: They comin' from way out—long distance. From the ends of the sky. It's the Lord and His weapons, bringin' smoke to wipe the land clean.
13.6: Start cryin' now—'cause the Day of the Lord? It right around the corner. And it ain't pretty—it's destruction comin' from the Almighty Himself.
13.7: Folk gon' be weak, hands fallin' limp. Every man's heart? Melted.
13.8: Panic everywhere. They gon' hurt like a woman in labor—scared, confused, facin' each other with fire in they eyes.
13.9: That Day of the Lord comin' hard—wrathful, full of fury. The land gon' be empty. The sinners? Wiped out.
13.10: Even the skies gon' go dark. Stars stop shinin'. Sun won't rise right. The moon ain't bringin' no light either.
13.11: God said, "I'm comin' for the whole world's evil. All the wickedness? It's gettin' dealt with. I'm stoppin' the arrogant in their tracks, and I'm knockin' down every proud and ruthless person."
13.12: "People gon' be so rare, they worth more than gold—like real Ophir gold type rare."
13.13: "I'm shakin' the skies. The whole earth gon' tremble, 'cause the Lord of Armies mad mad. When that anger drops—it's over."
13.14: Folks gon' run like hunted deer. Scattered sheep. Everybody runnin' to their own tribe, tryin' to get home.
13.15: If they catch you? You gettin' stabbed. If you captured? You ain't makin' it.
13.16: Babies gon' be killed in front of their parents. Homes robbed. Wives violated. It's ugly.
13.17: God said, "Look, I'm raisin' up the Medes against y'all. And they don't want your silver or gold—can't bribe 'em."
13.18: "They bowin' down nobody. Young men? Killed without hesitation. Babies? No mercy. Women? No compassion."
13.19: Babylon—you was the pride of nations. Chaldeans' crown jewel. But you gon' fall just like Sodom and Gomorrah when God set it off.
13.20: Ain't nobody livin' there again. Ever. No generations, no nomads settin' up tents, no shepherds keepin' sheep there.
13.21: Just wild creatures takin' over. Houses filled with owls. Ostriches movin' in. Wild goats doin' they thing.
13.22: Hyenas gon' be howlin' in the old palaces. Jackals chillin' in what used to be luxury. It's over for Babylon. Her clock tickin'. Time almost up. God said what He said.

14.1: God still got love for Jacob. He chose Israel, and He not changin' up. He settin' them back in their land, and even outsiders gon' want in—stickin' close to the house of Jacob.
14.2: Other nations gon' help bring them back home. And Israel? They gon' flip the script—rulin' over the ones who used to rule them. The oppressed now got the crown.
14.3: When the Lord finally gives you rest from all that pain, fear, and slavery…
14.4: You gon' start speakin' on the fall of Babylon's king like: "So it's over now? The bully shut up? The gold city finally gone?"
14.5: "God snapped the rod that the wicked held. That stick of control? Broken."
14.6: "He used to strike down nations, nonstop anger—now he gettin' stomped, and nobody stoppin' it."
14.7: "The whole world breathin' again. Peace everywhere. Songs breakin' out."
14.8: "Even the trees—cypress and cedar—out here rejoicin'. Talkin' 'bout, 'Since you fell, nobody came to chop us down.'"
14.9: "Hell itself been anticipatin' your arrival. The dead gettin' hype. All them past kings gettin' up off they thrones like, 'Oh, so you here now?'"
14.10: "They all starin' at you like, 'Dang… you weak now, too? Just like us?'"
14.11: "Your pride brought low to the grave. No more music, no more luxury—just worms under you, maggots coverin' you."
14.12: "How you fall like that, Lucifer? Son of the morning? You was up high, now you laid out. You used to weaken nations, now look at you."
14.13: "You had big dreams: 'I'ma rise to heaven, I'ma sit above God's stars, I'ma sit up top with the gods, I'ma be just like the Most High.'"
14.14: "You was tryna level up past the clouds, thinkin' you was untouchable."
14.15: "But nah. You headed straight to the pit—deep, dark, no exits."
14.16: "Folks gon' walk by lookin' like, 'This the one who shook the earth? Who wrecked kingdoms?"
14.17: "He turned the world to rubble, destroyed cities, and never opened the jails. Kept everybody locked up."
14.18: "Other kings at least get buried with honor.
14.19: "But you? Thrown outta your grave like trash. Like a bloody shirt from a soldier cut down. Tossed aside like a body nobody wanna touch."
14.20: "You don't get a king's funeral—'cause you destroyed your people and your land. Your fam line? Wiped clean. Nobody gon' mention y'all again."
14.21: "Prepare for their sons to be taken out too. Don't let that wicked legacy rise up and build cities again. Shut it all down."
14.22: God said, "I'm risin' up against Babylon. I'ma wipe out their name, their people, their future—all of it."
14.23: "I'ma turn that place into a swampy wasteland, full of wild animals. I'ma sweep it away like trash."
14.24: The Lord of Armies made a promise: "If I said it, it's gon' happen. Ain't no rewrites."
14.25: "I'ma crush Assyria in My land—step on 'em in My mountains. And that burden on My people? Gone."
14.26: "This ain't just about one country. This is My plan for the whole world.
14.27: "Who can stop Me? Who got the strength to push back My hand?"
14.28: This message came the year King Ahaz died:
14.29: "Philistia, don't get cocky just 'cause the one who hit you is gone. His replacement worse. Out the roots of that snake comes a venomous serpent. And his child? A fiery flying one."
14.30: "But My poor people? They gon' eat. They gon' rest. But your roots? I'ma starve 'em. Your remnant? Gone."
14.31: "Cry all you want, Philistine cities. Smoke comin' from the north. And when it hits? Ain't nobody gon' be missin' they mark."
14.32: What's the message for the world? That God Himself built Zion. And the poor, the outcasts, the overlooked? They safe in Him.

15.1: This the heavy word about Moab: In the dead of night, Ar done got wiped out—gone. Same night, Kir fell too—completely destroyed.
15.2: Moab's runnin' to their temples, cryin' at their altars. They up on Dibon's high places weepin'. They mournin' over Nebo, cryin' over Medeba. Everybody shaved bald, beards cut off—signs of straight-up grief.
15.3: Folks out in the streets rockin' sackcloth. They on rooftops, in the alleyways, Wailin' loud with bitter tears.
15.4: Heshbon and Elealeh join in—they screamin' so loud, folks hear it all the way in Jahaz. Even Moab's soldiers cryin' out now. Life feel too heavy for them to even carry.
15.5: "My heart hurt for Moab," Isaiah says. Their people runnin'—headed for Zoar like scared calves. On the road to Luhith, they goin' up cryin'. On the path to Horonaim, the cry of destruction echo loud.
15.6: Even the waters of Nimrim dried up. Grass dead. Land dead. Nothin' green left.
15.7: All they riches, all that stash they been holdin'? They packin' it up and takin' it with 'em—haulin' it to the Brook of the Willows.
15.8: The scream of Moab stretchin' out to every corner— Eglaim hearin' it, Beer Elim feelin' it.
15.9: Dimon's waters? Drenched in blood. But God said that ain't even the worst of it— He sendin' lions too. Whoever tryna escape Moab's fall? Them lions waitin'. Even the leftovers in the land ain't safe.

16.1: Send a lamb as tribute to Judah's king—from Sela in the wilderness all the way to Mount Zion.
16.2: Moab's daughters gon' be like birds flung from the nest—scared and scattered by the river crossings near Arnon.
16.3: "Yo, take advice, make it make sense. Be a safe shadow in the heat of the day. Hide the outcasts. Don't sell out the ones runnin' for their lives."
16.4: "Let My refugees stay with you, Moab. Be a safe zone from the destruction." 'Cause the oppressor? Done. Devastation? Wrappin' up. The destroyer? Already on his way out.
16.5: A new throne gon' be set up in mercy. Someone legit, sittin' in David's tent, ruling right—judging fair, movin' with speed and righteousness.
16.6: Yeah, we heard about Moab's ego—man got too much pride. Loud, arrogant, angry... But it's all talk. That stuff ain't holdin' up.
16.7: So Moab gon' cry for Moab. Everybody mournin'. Kir Hareseth's foundations? Cracked. The city feelin' that hit hard.
16.8: Heshbon's fields? Dried up. Sibmah's vineyard? Stripped bare. Foreign kings came in and crushed the best vines— They stretched all the way to Jazer, reached through the wilderness, even tryna stretch across the sea.
16.9: And I'm weepin' for Sibmah like Jazer did. Tears floodin' Heshbon and Elealeh. Why? 'Cause war just snatched their harvest. No more summer fruit. No joy in the fields.
16.10: Celebration's canceled. Ain't no music, no harvest songs, no stompin' grapes in the winepress. I personally hit the mute button on all that.
16.11: That's why my heart sound like a sad harp for Moab. Deep down, I feel it for Kir Heres.
16.12: Moab gon' be exhausted—cryin' on high places, runnin' to their idols. But all them prayers? Ain't gon' work. No answers comin'.
16.13: This ain't new. God already spoke this over Moab a while back.
16.14: But now He's stampin' it with a date: "In three years, like a contract with a hired worker, Moab's glory gon' be dust. All that population? Shrunk. All that pride? Gone. What's left? A weak, tiny remnant—barely hangin' on."

17.1: This the message against Damascus: "Look—Damascus gon' stop bein' a city. It's 'bout to be straight ruins."
17.2: Aroer's towns? Ghost towns now. Flocks just chillin' there, sleepin' peaceful. Ain't nobody around to bother 'em.
17.3: No more strongholds in Ephraim. Damascus lost its crown too. Syria gon' fade just like Israel did—temporary glory that didn't last," says the Lord of Heaven's Armies.
17.4: "In that day," God says, "Jacob's shine gon' dim. The fat of the land gon' dry up."
17.5: "It's gon' feel like harvesters cuttin' grain—only a few heads left. Like folks sweepin' the Valley of Rephaim for scraps."
17.6: "A few grapes still hangin'—like when you shake an olive tree and just two or three clingin' to the top branch. That's all that's left," says the Lord God of Israel.
17.7: But in that day, people gon' finally look up—to the One who made 'em. Eyes gon' lock on the Holy One of Israel.
17.8: They ain't gon' be worshipin' idols no more. No more statues, no handmade gods, no incense burnin' to blocks of wood.
17.9: All them cities they used to trust in? Abandoned like a dead tree limb. Left empty. No one comin' back.
17.10: "Why? 'Cause y'all forgot the God who saved y'all. Didn't even check in with the Rock that held you down. You out here plantin' foreign seeds, settin' up nice lil' gardens,
17.11: Tryin' to grow success overnight. But when harvest time hits? It's all rubble. Just pain and sorrow waitin' for you."
17.12: "Woe to all them loud nations—roarin' like ocean waves, Rushin' in deep like floodwaters."
17.13: "Yeah, they sound scary, but I'ma check 'em. God gon' speak, and they gon' scatter like dust on a windy mountain. They gon' roll away like tumbleweeds in a storm."
17.14: "Come evening? Trouble rollin' in. But by sunrise? It's all over. That's what happens to anybody who tried to rob us— That's their fate. That's what they get."

18.1: Woe to that land full of buzzing wings, Way out past the rivers of Ethiopia (Cush),
18.2: The one sendin' out slick ambassadors on papyrus boats, Sayin': "Go, messengers! Go holla at that tall, smooth-skinned nation, That people known for their strength since way back, A nation that been pressin' folks and claimin' territory— Land where rivers slice the land up."
18.3: Listen up, everybody on earth: When God raises His banner up on the mountains—you gon' see it. When He blow that trumpet—you gon' hear it.
18.4: The Lord told me: "I'm chillin'. Watchin' from above. Like the heat shimmerin' on a sunny day, Like morning dew sittin' quiet during harvest."
18.5: But before that harvest hits, Right when the bud lookin' good and the grapes start ripenin'— Snip! God pull out the pruning shears. He cuttin' off branches and takin' 'em down.
18.6: What's left? Birds of prey gon' feast all summer. Beasts of the wild gon' post up all winter. Bodies left in the open—no burial, no honor.
18.7: But hold up— In that time, a gift gon' come to the Lord of Armies. From that same tall, smooth-skinned people, From that same powerful nation that used to strike fear, From the land divided by rivers. And that gift? They bringin' it to Mount Zion, To where God's name stay lifted.

19.1: This the word against Egypt: Look, the Lord ridin' in on a fast cloud, Touchin' down in Egypt like, boom. All them Egyptian idols shakin'. The people's hearts? Meltin' inside they chest.
19.2: "I'ma have Egyptians turn on each other. Brother against brother. Neighbor against neighbor. City fightin' city. Kingdom beefin' with kingdom."
19.3: "Their whole spirit gon' collapse. I'ma shut down all their wisdom. They gon' run to idols, charmers, psychics, and witchcraft for answers."
19.4: "And then I'ma let a cruel master rule over them. A cold king gon' take charge," says the Lord of Heaven's Armies.
19.5: The sea gon' dry up. The river? Wasteland.
19.6: Streams turn nasty. Canals? Dry bones. Reeds and rushes? Dead.
19.7: The papyrus by the Nile? Gone. Crops by the river? Withered up and blown away.
19.8: Fishermen cryin'. Ain't no more hooks in the Nile, no nets workin'.
19.9: The folks who weave fine linens? Embarrassed. Industry shut down.
19.10: The foundation of the hustle—broken. Everybody tryna get a check? Hurtin' deep in they soul.
19.11: Them leaders in Zoan? Dumb. Pharaoh's "wise men"? Givin' foolish advice. Y'all really out here tellin' Pharaoh, "I'm wise. I'm royalty"? Please.
19.12: Where they at now? Tell us, if y'all so smart— What's God plannin' for Egypt?
19.13: Zoan's leaders? Played. Noph's crew? Fooled. These big-time officials led Egypt straight off the cliff.
19.14: God mixed a twisted spirit into the nation, Now they out here movin' like a drunk dude trippin' in his own throw up.
19.15: Ain't nobody workin'. Top or bottom, high or low, palm branch or reed—no jobs.
19.16: That day, Egypt gon' be shaky— Like scared little girls, flinchin' every time God lifts His hand.
19.17: Just hearin' "Judah" gon' make 'em nervous, 'Cause they know what God got planned.
19.18: On that day? Five cities in Egypt gon' speak Hebrew and rep the Lord of Armies. One of 'em gon' be called "The City of Destruction."
19.19: And in the middle of Egypt? An altar to God. At the border? A pillar for the Lord.
19.20: Both gon' be signs—a witness to the Lord in Egypt. When they cry out 'cause they gettin' pressed, God gon' send a Savior. A real one. A Mighty One. He gon' step in and save them.
19.21: That's when Egypt finally gon' know the Lord. They gon' offer Him sacrifice, make vows, and actually keep them.
19.22: God gon' strike them—but He also gon' heal them. They gon' turn back to Him, And He gon' respond with mercy and restoration.
19.23: In that day? A highway from Egypt to Assyria. Egyptians gon' travel to Assyria, Assyrians gon' pull up in Egypt, And they gon' serve God together.
19.24: On that day, it won't just be about Israel. It'll be Egypt, Assyria, and Israel—one squad, A blessing in the middle of the land.
19.25: God gon' bless all three like: "Egypt—My people. Assyria—My handiwork. Israel—My inheritance."

20.1: So in the year Tartan rolled up on Ashdod (Sargon, king of Assyria, sent him to handle business—and he took that city),
20.2: God told Isaiah, "Take off your sackcloth. Slide off your sandals." Isaiah did it—walked around barefoot and straight-up naked.
20.3: Then the Lord said, "Just like Isaiah walked around lookin' wild—naked and barefoot for three whole years as a sign—I'ma let y'all know what's comin' for Egypt and Ethiopia."
20.4: "The king of Assyria gon' snatch up Egyptians and Ethiopians—young and old—walkin' 'em out barefoot, stripped down, exposed. Backs out. Shame on full display."
20.5: The folks who were trustin' in Ethiopia's strength and Egypt's shine? They gon' be embarrassed. Shook.
20.6: And everybody in the region gon' be sayin', "Dang... we really thought they was gon' save us. Now we runnin' talkin' 'bout who gon' help us escape Assyria? If they got taken down like that—what hope we got?"

21.1: Message against the "Wilderness by the Sea": A storm's blowin' in from the desert—hot, wild, violent. Trouble comin' from a rough place.
21.2: This vision hittin' me hard. Betrayers stay betrayin'. Thieves stay robbin'. Elam—get ready. Media—tighten up and attack. God say He finna shut down Babylon's cries.
21.3: Man, this got me twisted up inside. My stomach hurt like labor pains. I was shook when I heard it. I froze when I saw it.
21.4: My heart racin', fear grippin' me. The night I thought would bring peace? Now it got me spooked.
21.5: Set the table, y'all. Post the guards. Feast if you want—but y'all better armor up. Anoint the shield—it's goin' down.
21.6: God told me: "Put a watchman on duty. Tell him to speak what he sees."
21.7: He saw it—a chariot pulled by horses. Donkeys. Camels. Troops movin' in. He watched close.
21.8: Then the watchman cried, "Yo! A lion! I been up on this tower day and night. Eyes open. And now—
21.9: Look, I see them ridin' in!" Then he said: "Babylon done fell. She fell for real. And all her fake gods? Smashed into the dirt."
21.10: My people, the ones threshed like grain— This is what I heard from the Lord of Heaven's Armies, And I'm tellin' it straight to you.
21.11: Message about Dumah (aka Edom): Somebody callin' me from Seir: "Watchman, what's good with the night? What's comin'?"
21.12: I said: "The morning comin', but night ain't over. You got questions? Ask. But you gon' have to come back again."
21.13: Message about Arabia: Y'all nomads from Dedan campin' out in the forest?
21.14: Tema's people—go bring water to the thirsty. Hand bread to them who been runnin'.
21.15: They runnin' from the sword, from war, From drawn bows and destruction.
21.16: The Lord told me: "In one year—just like a hired worker's contract— Kedar's glory gon' fade.
21.17: Them archers, them warriors? Most of 'em gone. God, the Lord of Israel, said it—and He don't miss."

22.1: Message to the Valley of Vision (aka Jerusalem): Why y'all actin' up on the rooftops? What's really goin' on?
22.2: This city loud, turnt up, actin' like it's a celebration— But your people ain't even dyin' in battle. They droppin' in shame.
22.3: Your leaders ran off together, But they got caught—archers got 'em. Folks in the city? Snatched and chained. Didn't matter how far they came from.
22.4: I said, "Man, don't even look at me. I'm cryin' for real. Don't try to comfort me— This is heartbreak for my people."
22.5: This right here a day of confusion, breakdown, and chaos, And it's comin' straight from the Lord God of Heaven's Armies. Walls fallin'. Screams echoin' off the mountains.
22.6: Elam rollin' deep with chariots and bows. Kir showin' up with shields ready.
22.7: The valleys? Full of war gear. Horsemen lined up at your gates.
22.8: God took away Judah's protection. And y'all? Instead of lookin' to Him, You ran to go dig through the royal armory.
22.9: Y'all saw how bad the city of David was hurt. Started collectin' water like it was gonna save you.
22.10: Counted your houses, Tore some down to build up your wall.
22.11: Built a water system between the walls to hold it down… But you ain't look back to the One who made it all. You ain't even acknowledge the One who set this up long ago.
22.12: God was callin' for tears, mourning, humility, People to humble themselves—sackcloth and all.
22.13: But instead? Y'all was out here throwin' parties: Slayin' oxen, grillin' sheep, drinkin' wine, talkin' 'bout: "Let's eat and drink, 'cause tomorrow we dead anyway."
22.14: And God whispered in my ear: "This sin right here? Ain't no forgiveness for it. Not in this life. Not before death." Says the Lord of Hosts.
22.15: The Lord said: "Go talk to Shebna, the dude over the palace. Tell him:
22.16: Who you think you are, carvin' out a fancy tomb for yourself? Like you royalty or somethin'?"
22.17: "Watch this— God gon' grab you up,
22.18: Twist you like a ball, And toss you far out the land. You gon' die out there. All them chariots you flexin'? They gon' be a disgrace to your people."
22.19: "You done. I'm takin' you out your seat, Pullin' you from power."
22.20: "That day, I'ma call Eliakim—son of Hilkiah.
22.21: He gettin' your robe, your belt, your role. I'm handin' him the keys. He gon' lead with heart—like a father to Judah and Jerusalem."
22.22: "I'ma put the key to David's house on his shoulder. If he open it? Can't nobody close it. If he close it? It's closed for real."
22.23: "He gon' be like a strong peg nailed in tight. A whole throne of honor for his fam."
22.24: "All the weight of his household— Every dish, every bowl— It's hangin' on him."
22.25: But even that peg— That strong one? One day it's comin' down. It gon' snap. The burden fall. Because the Lord said so.

23.1: "Cry out, Tarshish ships! Tyre been wiped out—no more houses, no more harbor. Word hit from Cyprus, and folks shook."
23.2: "Be quiet, y'all on the coast—especially you Sidon merchants, livin' off them seafarin' deals."
23.3: "Tyre was makin' bank off grain floatin' in from Egypt, off river harvests—she was everybody's go-to market."
23.4: "Sidon, hang your head. Even the sea speakin' now, sayin': 'I ain't raised no babies or built no future. I ain't birthin' no legacies.'"
23.5: "When Egypt hear the news? They gon' be in deep pain—can't believe Tyre took that L."
23.6: "Run on to Tarshish, coast folks! Start cryin'—your hub just collapsed."
23.7: "Y'all remember how lit Tyre used to be? That ancient city, movin' like royalty? Now she lookin' lost."
23.8: "Who flipped the script on Tyre? The one city where merchants moved like princes and ran the trade game with global respect?"
23.9: "God did. The Lord of Heaven's Armies. He brought down all that pride, all that global glory—turned it into shame."
23.10: "Tarshish, your land gon' be wide open—no more gates, no more might. Just floodin' out."
23.11: "God reached over the sea, shook up whole kingdoms. He gave the word: Canaan's strongholds gotta fall."
23.12: "And He said, 'Sidon, daughter tryna stay pretty while sufferin'? You ain't gon' celebrate no more. Go run to Cyprus—won't be no peace for you there either.'"
23.13: "Look at Babylon—land of the Chaldeans. They wasn't even a thing at first! Assyria built it up just for wild animals to take over later. They raised towers, palaces—then let it fall."
23.14: "Cry out again, ships of Tarshish—your stronghold? Wrecked."
23.15: "And listen, Tyre gon' be forgotten for seventy years—like one king's whole lifetime. But after them years up, she comin' back like the song say…"
23.16: "'Grab your harp, sis—walk the city like an old-school harlot. Play your tunes, sing loud, try to get folks to remember you again.'"
23.17: "After them seventy years, the Lord gon' let Tyre go back to hustlin'—tradin' with every kingdom out there, flirtin' with the whole world again."
23.18: "But this time, her money gon' be holy. She ain't stackin' it up for herself no more—it's all goin' to those who live before the Lord. They gon' eat good and stay fresh in fine clothes."

24.1: Look now—God 'bout to clear the whole earth out. He flippin' the land upside down and scatterin' everybody everywhere.
24.2: Don't matter who you are—priest or people, servant or master, employee or boss, buyer or seller, lender or borrower—ain't nobody exempt.
24.3: The whole land gon' be emptied out and looted. Why? 'Cause God said so. Period.
24.4: The earth mournin' and dryin' up. The world lookin' weak. Even the ones who thought they was on top feelin' it now.
24.5: Earth messed up 'cause of the folks in it—they broke God's rules, switched up the order, and disrespected the eternal covenant.
24.6: That's why the curse eatin' up the land, and folks feelin' the heat. Burned out. Only a few gon' be left standin'.
24.7: Ain't no more turnin' up—wine runnin' out, vines dyin', and happy folks out here groanin'.
24.8: The tambourines done gone quiet. The party noise done stopped. Ain't no more joy in them instruments.
24.9: Don't nobody even wanna sip no more—the liquor got a bitter aftertaste. Ain't no vibes.
24.10: The city confused and broke down. Houses boarded up—ain't nobody comin' in or out.
24.11: Folks out in the streets cryin' for wine, but joy gone. The whole land just heavy now.
24.12: City's a ghost town. Even the gate fallin' apart.
24.13: What's left of the people? They like the last olives clingin' to a tree or a couple grapes missed in the harvest. Just scraps.
24.14: But even in all this, a few gon' raise they voice and praise God from far away.
24.15: So go 'head and glorify the Lord in the early light—shout His name from the coastlines and across the seas.
24.16: From every corner of the earth, we hear it: "Glory to the righteous!" But me? I'm wrecked. Woe to me. These folks out here movin' foul—backstabbin' on a whole 'nother level.
24.17: Fear, traps, and pits waitin' on y'all, people of the earth. Ain't no escape.
24.18: You run from fear? You fall in a pit. Climb out that pit? Boom—you caught in a trap. Heaven openin' up, earth's foundation shakin' like it can't hold on.
24.19: The earth breakin' down bad. Split wide open. Shakin' like it's in a full-on meltdown.
24.20: It's wobblin' like a drunk, leanin' like a raggedy shack. All that sin weighin' it down—it's fallin' and ain't gettin' back up.
24.21: When that day hit, God comin' for the big shots—both heavenly and earthly. Ain't nobody safe.
24.22: They gon' be rounded up like inmates, locked down in the pit. After a while, the judgment still gon' hit.
24.23: Even the moon and sun gon' be embarrassed when God shows up in glory—reignin' from Zion, holdin' court in Jerusalem, lookin' majestic in front of His people.

25.1: Lord, You my God. I'ma lift You up, praise Your name, 'cause You been doin' big things. Everything You planned back then? Faithful and true, no cap.
25.2: You turned a whole city into rubble. That stronghold? Gone. That foreign palace? Ain't never comin' back.
25.3: That's why even strong nations gon' respect You. Big cities that used to act scary? They gon' fear You now.
25.4: You been a shelter for the broke and hurting. A safe spot in the storm. A cool shade in the heat. When the loud and wild ones tried it, You held it down like a strong wall.
25.5: You gon' shut them noisy oppressors up—like heat disappearing when a cloud rolls in. Their song? Fadin' out.
25.6: And right here on this mountain, the Lord gon' throw a feast for everybody. We talkin' rich food, real wine, no cheap stuff—choice cuts, full flavor, perfectly aged.
25.7: On this mountain, He takin' off the cover that been blockin' all the people. That heavy veil over the nations? Ripped away.
25.8: Death? He swallowin' it whole. Tears? Wiped from every face. Shame? Gone from His people—all across the earth. God done said it, and that's that.
25.9: In that day folks gon' say, "This right here is our God! We waited on Him, and He showed up! This the Lord! We waited, and now we rejoicin'—He saved us for real!"
25.10: God's hand gon' rest right here on this mountain. But Moab? He gon' stomp them down like straw gettin' trampled in a dirty pile.
25.11: They gon' reach out tryin' to swim through it, flailin' around—but He gon' drag that pride down. All them slick schemes they hands cooked up? Shut down.
25.12: That big ol' fortress wall? God knockin' it flat. Layin' it down in the dust—ain't gon' be nothin' left standin'.

26.1: On that day, Judah gon' be singin': "We got a strong city! God set up salvation like walls and defense all around us."
26.2: "Open up the gates—let the real ones in. The folks that stay true, that hold tight to God's ways."
26.3: You keep folks in perfect peace when they keep they mind on You—'cause they trust You for real.
26.4: Keep trustin' the Lord forever. In the Lord—Yah Himself—we got everlasting strength.
26.5: He brings down the high and mighty—the ones sittin' up in them lofty cities. He drop 'em to the ground, all the way to the dirt.
26.6: The poor and the lowly gon' step on what used to be high places. They walkin' on what used to walk on them.
26.7: God, You make the way straight for the ones who live right. You keep they steps steady and sure.
26.8: Lord, we been waitin' on You while You was movin' in judgment. Our soul just want Your name, Your presence, Your memory.
26.9: Even at night, I'm longin' for You. My spirit searchin' early. When You move in justice, the whole world gon' learn how to do right.
26.10: Even when You show the wicked grace, they still don't wanna act right. In a land full of righteousness, they still play dirty and ignore Your glory.
26.11: Lord, even when Your hand is lifted up, they act like they can't see it. But they gon' see eventually—shame gon' hit 'em hard. Jealousy gon' burn, and Your fire gon' finish what it started.
26.12: Lord, You the one who brings us peace. Every good thing we ever did—You was the one behind it.
26.13: God, other masters had us in chains before, but we only speak Your name now. You the only one we honor.
26.14: Them old rulers? Dead and gone. They not comin' back. You wiped them out and erased the memory of 'em.
26.15: You been growin the nation, Lord. You done made Your name big. You stretched the borders and showed out.
26.16: When times got hard, we came runnin' back to You. We poured our hearts out when You checked us.
26.17: We was like a woman in labor—cryin', strugglin', waitin' for the promise to come.
26.18: But all we gave birth to was wind. No breakthrough, no deliverance. The world stayed stuck, and we couldn't fix it.
26.19: But You said the dead gon' live. Our people who sleepin' in the dust gon' rise up. Wake up and sing, y'all—God's breath is like fresh dew, and the ground gon' give up the dead.
26.20: Come on, My people. Get inside, shut your doors, hide for a little while. Let God's anger pass through.
26.21: 'Cause the Lord steppin' out. He comin' to handle what's been done in secret. The earth gon' tell it all—every bit of blood spilled, every wrong that's been buried? It's all comin' to light.

27.1: When that day hit, the Lord gon' swing His heavy sword—sharp, strong, and mighty. He takin' down Leviathan, that slippery, twisty serpent. That sea monster? Yeah, God gon' finish it off.
27.2: On that day, somebody gon' start singin': "This right here is God's vineyard, red with new wine!"
27.3: The Lord say, "I'm the one who watches over her. I water her all the time. I don't let nobody mess with her—I'm on guard 24/7."
27.4: "Ain't no fury in Me. But if somebody try to throw thorns at Me, come at Me sideways? I'll burn it all down quick."
27.5: "But if they just grab hold of My strength, make peace with Me? Then we good. They can live in peace with Me."
27.6: God gon' help His people grow deep roots in Jacob. Israel gon' bloom, flourish, and spread fruit all over the world.
27.7: Did God hit Israel like He hit the nations that hit them? Nah. Did He wipe them out like He did the enemies? Nope.
27.8: God dealt with them gently, in doses. Like a strong wind He sent them away, but it wasn't to destroy—it was to correct.
27.9: That's how He gon' erase Jacob's guilt. That's the result of their sins gettin' removed: they gon' smash their altars to pieces—ain't no more idols standin' after that.
27.10: The cities that was once strong? Empty. Ain't nobody livin' there. Cows just chillin' where folks used to live, munchin' on the ruins.
27.11: The trees dried up, branches broken off. Women gatherin' 'em to burn. That's 'cause the people ain't got no sense. The One who made 'em ain't showin' 'em no mercy 'til they get it right.
27.12: But hold up—when that day come, the Lord gon' sweep the land like He threshin' wheat—from the Euphrates to the border of Egypt. And He gon' gather His people back, one by one.
27.13: A big ol' trumpet gon' sound off. Folks who was lost in Assyria, outcasts in Egypt—they gon' come back. They gon' show up in Jerusalem, worshippin' the Lord on His holy mountain.

28.1: Woe to y'all up in Ephraim, drunk off pride and liquor, rockin' that crown like you all that—y'all beauty fadin' fast like a flower on a hot day. Y'all sittin' high in them valleys, but y'all slippin'.
28.2: Look, the Lord ain't playin'. He got somebody strong comin'—like a hailstorm, a flood that don't quit. He finna slam y'all down with His own hand.
28.3: That proud crown the drunk folks in Ephraim rockin'? It's gon' be stomped on.
28.4: That glory they flexin'? Gon' fade like flowers. It's like a juicy grape picked too early—soon as somebody see it, they grab it and it's gone.
28.5: But when that day come, the Lord of Heaven's Armies gon' be the real crown of glory, shinin' for the leftovers, the faithful ones.
28.6: He gon' give justice to the judges, and power to the folks who stand strong at the gate, holdin' the line.
28.7: But even the priests and prophets drunk too. Wine got 'em twisted. They lost in the sauce, can't see straight, can't judge right.
28.8: The tables they sittin' at? Filthy. Vomit everywhere. Ain't a clean spot in sight.
28.9: And God's like, "Who I'ma teach? Babies fresh off milk? Toddlers just off the bottle?"
28.10: But they gotta learn slow—precept by precept, line by line, lil' here, lil' there.
28.11: So God gon' speak to 'em through foreign lips, other tongues, tryin' to get through to 'em.
28.12: He told 'em, "This the rest y'all need, this the peace I'm offerin'." But they ain't wanna listen.
28.13: So the Word hit 'em like this: Precept on precept, line on line, here a lil' there a lil'. But instead of growin', they trip and fall back. Now they trapped.
28.14: So hear this, y'all smug leaders in Jerusalem—the ones jokin' while runnin' the people into the ground:
28.15: Y'all think y'all got a deal with death? A pact with the grave? Y'all think y'all safe when disaster hits 'cause y'all hid behind lies and built bunkers of deception?
28.16: But the Lord God say, "Nah. I'm layin' a foundation in Zion—a tested stone, precious and solid. Whoever trusts in it ain't gon' panic."
28.17: God gon' measure with justice and righteousness. Lies? Gon' get swept away like floodwater. All that fake stuff? Exposed.
28.18: That contract y'all got with death? Void. That deal with the grave? Canceled. When the flood hits, y'all gettin' washed too.
28.19: Every time it sweeps by, it's takin' y'all. Mornin', night, over and over. Just hearin' 'bout it gon' give y'all chills.
28.20: The bed too short, y'all can't stretch out. The blanket too small, can't even cover up.
28.21: The Lord gon' rise up like He did at Perazim, wild like back in Gibeon. He comin' to do His strange, surprising work—judgment y'all ain't ready for.
28.22: So stop playin'! Don't keep mockin' or y'all chains gon' get tighter. I done heard from the Lord—destruction is comin' for the whole earth.
28.23: Now listen up—lean in and hear what I'm sayin'.
28.24: Does a farmer keep plowin' forever? Nah, he turns the soil, breaks it up, and then moves on.
28.25: When it's ready, he plants black cumin, cumin, wheat, barley, spelt—each in its own lane, all in order.
28.26: 'Cause God teaches him how to do it right. It's all divine wisdom.
28.27: You don't beat black cumin like you thresh wheat. It gets tapped with a stick. Cumin gets hit with a rod.
28.28: Bread flour gotta be ground down—but you don't crush it forever. Ain't no need to wreck the thing with wheels and horses.
28.29: This all comes from the Lord of Heaven's Armies. He's wise with His plans and flawless in how He guides.

29.1: Woe to Ariel—yeah, Ariel, the city where King David used to walk. Go 'head, keep countin' the years, keep havin' your lil' feasts.
29.2: But I'm gon' press you, Ariel. You gon' feel the weight. It's gon' get heavy with sorrow. But to Me? You still gon' be Ariel—My altar, My fire.
29.3: I'ma post up all around you, set up camp, dig in with trenches, build up walls—yeah, I'm comin' for you.
29.4: You gon' be brought low—real low. Talkin' from the dirt like whispers from the grave. Your voice gon' sound like you speakin' through dust.
29.5: And all them enemies comin' for you? Poof. Gone like fine powder in the wind. Them haters? Gon' blow away like ash. All that? Gon' shift in a second.
29.6: The Lord of Heaven's Armies gon' check y'all with thunder, earthquakes, loud noise, storms, hurricanes, and fire that don't quit.
29.7: All them nations tryin' to gang up on Ariel? They gon' vanish like a dream you can't remember.
29.8: It's gon' be like somebody dreamin' they eatin', but wake up still hungry. Or drinkin' in a dream, but wake up dry and thirsty. That's how all them nations gon' feel after tryin' to take Zion—empty and unsatisfied.
29.9: Y'all better stop and look. Be amazed—but y'all blind now. Y'all stumbling, not 'cause you drunk on wine, but 'cause your spirit off.
29.10: God done hit y'all with deep sleep. He shut the eyes of y'all prophets, put covers over the seers.
29.11: Now the whole vision like a sealed book. You hand it to someone who can read and say, "Hey, read this," but they like, "I can't—it's sealed."
29.12: Then you hand it to someone who can't read and say, "Read this," and they like, "I don't even know how."
29.13: So God say: "These folks talk like they close to Me, but their hearts? Way off. They honor Me with their mouths, but they just follow rules taught by people—not Me."
29.14: So I'ma shake things up again. Gon' do something wild—blow y'all minds. Them so-called wise men? Gon' lose their wisdom. All that knowledge? Vanish.
29.15: Woe to the ones tryin' to hide their moves from God, thinkin' they slick in the dark—like, "Ain't nobody seein' me. Ain't nobody knowin'."
29.16: Uh-uh, y'all flipped it all backwards. The clay don't tell the potter, "You ain't make me." The creation can't clown the Creator talkin' 'bout, "He don't know nothin'."
29.17: But don't trip—it ain't gon' be long. Lebanon gon' be like fertile fields again. Them fields gon' rise up like forests.
29.18: In that day, even the deaf gon' hear the words in the book. The blind gon' see light bustin' through their darkness.
29.19: The humble gon' have real joy in the Lord, and the poor gon' celebrate the Holy One of Israel.
29.20: The bullies? Done. The mockers? Canceled. And the folks always lookin' to catch somebody slippin'? They out.
29.21: The ones tryna trap people with their words, tryna get folks in trouble just for speakin' truth—God gon' deal with them too.
29.22: So the Lord who saved Abraham got a word for Jacob's fam: "Jacob ain't gotta be ashamed no more. Ain't gotta hide his face in shame."
29.23: When he sees his kids—My handiwork—he gon' honor My name. They gon' lift up the Holy One of Jacob and revere the God of Israel.
29.24: Even the ones who been lost in the sauce gon' catch some wisdom. The complainers? They finna learn for real.

30.1: "Woe to my hard-headed children," says the Lord. "Y'all makin' plans without checkin' in with Me. Y'all movin' in your own spirit, not Mine—stackin' sin on top of sin.
30.2: Runnin' off to Egypt lookin' for backup, without even askin' Me first. Trustin' Pharaoh like he got you covered. Believin' Egypt gon' keep you safe in the shadows.
30.3: But Pharaoh's 'strength'? That's gon' be your embarrassment. Egypt's protection? That's gon' be your downfall.
30.4: Look, his crew sittin' in Zoan, his messengers posted in Hanes—
30.5: And what good did they do you? Nada. Egypt ain't bring no help. Just shame and disappointment."
30.6: This the word on the wild south: trouble, danger, lions and serpents on the road. And here y'all go haulin' riches on donkeys, gold on camels—draggin' treasure to folks who can't do nothin' for you.
30.7: Egypt? Ain't worth it. Helpin' in vain. I call her "Rahab Who Just Sits There"—all bark, no bite.
30.8: God said, "Write it down. Put it on the record. Don't let 'em forget this."
30.9: "These folks rebellious—straight-up liars. They won't even listen when I speak.
30.10: They tell the prophets, 'Stop tellin' us the truth! We want smooth talk—tell us somethin' nice. Lie if you got to.'
30.11: 'Move out the way. Don't bring that Holy One of Israel talk to us no more.'"
30.12: So the Lord, the Holy One, says: "Since y'all reject My word and put your trust in oppression and crookedness,
30.13: You gon' fall like a cracked wall—one good shake, and boom—it all comes down, quick.
30.14: And when it falls, it's gon' shatter like a clay pot, no piece big enough to scoop a coal or dip out water."
30.15: The Lord God said: "Your salvation was always in returning to Me, in quiet rest and trust. That's where your strength was." But nah—you ain't want that.
30.16: Y'all said, "Nah, we ridin' out on horses!" Alright, then ride. But your enemies gon' be even faster.
30.17: A thousand of y'all gon' run from one enemy. Five folks chase y'all down till only one pole standin' on a hill, waivin' like a white flag.
30.18: But God? He waitin'. Waitin' to show y'all grace. He still gon' be exalted—still full of mercy. The Lord is fair. Blessed are the ones who just wait on Him.
30.19: Y'all gon' live in Zion again, and no more tears. He'll hear you when you cry—and answer.
30.20: Even when you go through hard times—eatin' the bread of pain and drinkin' struggle—your teachers won't be hidden no more. You gon' see clearly.
30.21: And you gon' hear a voice behind you sayin', "This the way. Walk in it," whether you turn left or right.
30.22: You gon' throw away your idols like trash—silver and gold images? Gone. You gon' be like, "Ugh! Get this mess outta here!"
30.23: Then God gon' send rain for your seeds. Your land gon' give you big harvests. Your cattle gon' eat good in wide pastures.
30.24: Even your work animals gon' get fancy feed—clean, sifted grain.
30.25: Streams gon' flow from every mountain on the day when the towers fall and the enemy gets crushed.
30.26: The moon gon' shine like the sun. The sun? Seven times brighter—like a full week of daylight in one. That's when God starts patchin' y'all up, healin' the wounds.
30.27: Look! The name of the Lord comin' from far off, burnin' with anger. His words heavy, His mouth full of fire,
30.28: His breath like a flood reachin' high—siftin' nations like flour, puttin' a bit in their mouths to steer 'em off course.
30.29: But you? You gon' have a praise song, like festival nights, like a joyful march to the mountain of God, with music in your soul.
30.30: God gon' speak LOUD. His arm comin' down with power—fire, storm, and hail. You gon' feel it.
30.31: Assyria? They gon' get beat just from hearin' His voice.
30.32: Every strike God land? It'll come with tambourines and harps playin'. A whole divine beatdown, but with rhythm.
30.33: That fire pit called Tophet? Already built—real deep and wide. Plenty of firewood. The Lord's breath gon' light it up like a blast of hot sulfur.

31.1: Woe to the ones runnin' down to Egypt for help. Trustin' in horses 'cause they deep, Relyin' on chariots 'cause they flashy, Thinkin' them riders strong enough to save them— But ain't even lookin' up to the Holy One of Israel. Ain't even tryna check in with the Lord.
31.2: But God? He ain't slow, He wise. He gon' bring the smoke, and His word ain't comin' back empty. He gon' stand up against the evildoers And the folks givin' them shady help.
31.3: Egypt? They just people—not God. Their horses? Made of flesh—not spirit. So when God stretch out His hand, Both the one helpin' and the one bein' helped? They both gon' fall. All of 'em goin' down together.
31.4: The Lord said, "When I pull up, it's gon' be like a lion standin' over its prey— Growlin' deep, unbothered. Let the shepherds make noise if they want to, I ain't moved. I ain't scared. I'm fightin' for Mount Zion. I'm fightin' for My people."
31.5: Just like birds swoopin' down to protect their nest, That's how the Lord gon' guard Jerusalem. He'll defend it, deliver it, and cover it— Won't let it fall.
31.6: Y'all need to turn back to the One y'all turned your back on— Y'all done did Him dirty for real.
31.7: But when that day hit, Everybody gon' toss them gold and silver idols like garbage. All that mess y'all made with your own hands? Gone.
31.8: Assyria gon' fall— Not by some regular man's sword, But by a sword they ain't ready for. They gon' run, Their soldiers gon' be forced to work like slaves.
31.9: Their leader? He gon' be shook, retreatin' to his fortress. His top men? Terrified of the banner—terrified of God's presence. The Lord speaks: "My fire burnin' in Zion, And My furnace stay lit in Jerusalem."

32.1: Look, a real King gon' step up and rule right, And His crew? They gon' lead with justice, not just titles.
32.2: That kind of man gon' be like shelter from the storm, Like water in a dry place, Like shade when the sun out here doin' the most— Peace in a wild world.
32.3: Folks gon' start seein' clearly, no more blind eyes. And ears? They actually gon' listen.
32.4: Even the reckless hearts gon' slow down and learn, And the ones who used to stutter? They gon' speak truth clear and bold.
32.5: You ain't gon' see fools gettin' called "generous" no more, And stingy folks won't be fakin' like they got good hearts.
32.6: 'Cause fools talk nonsense, They stay up to no good— Doin' dirty in the name of God, Letting the hungry stay hungry, And blockin' folks from gettin' even a sip.
32.7: The shady ones? Always plottin' on the poor, Lyin' just to keep them down, Even when the needy speak truth.
32.8: But the one with a real heart? He stay thinkin' up ways to bless others, And his blessings gon' keep him solid.
32.9: Y'all chillin' too hard— You women sittin' easy, listen up. Complacent daughters? This message for you too.
32.10: In just over a year, Y'all gon' feel that pressure— No grapes, no harvest, no good times.
32.11: Shake in your boots, you laid-back ladies. Take off the glam, throw on sackcloth, It's mourning season.
32.12: Folks gon' beat their chests in sorrow 'Cause the good fields dry up, Ain't no fruit on the vine.
32.13: The land? Gon' be filled with thorns and mess. Even the spots that used to be poppin'—quiet.
32.14: Mansions left empty, City vibes gone, It's just wild donkeys and sheep hangin' out now.
32.15: But hold up— When the Spirit comes down from on high, That desert gon' bloom. The dry field gon' turn lush, And the lush gon' grow like a forest.
32.16: Justice gon' set up camp in them dry places, And righteousness? It's gon' live out in the new growth.
32.17: When righteousness does its thing, It brings peace— Not just quiet, but that deep-down, ain't-worried kinda peace.
32.18: My people gon' live in real safety, Homes locked down with rest and calm vibes.
32.19: Even if the storm hits and takes down the forest, And the city takes a hit too— We gon' still be good.
32.20: Blessed are the ones sowin' seeds by every stream, Lettin' the ox and donkey roam free, 'Cause they ain't scared to keep it movin' and keep it flowin'.

33.1: Woe to you shady folks— You been robbin' folks, but ain't never been robbed yourself. You double-crossin' people, But soon as you stop? They gon' double-cross you right back.
33.2: Lord, come through for us. We been waitin' on You. Be our strength every morning, Our way out when trouble shows up.
33.3: When the chaos hit, folks gon' run scared. The moment You rise up? Nations gon' scatter like roaches when the lights cut on.
33.4: The stuff they stole? Gon' get picked clean— Like locusts sweepin' through a field.
33.5: God sittin' high and lifted— He posted up in heaven. Zion full of justice and right now 'cause of Him.
33.6: Wisdom and knowledge? That's your real security these days. Salvation your foundation. And fearin' the Lord? That's the real treasure.
33.7: Even the bravest out here cryin' in the streets. The peace-talkers got nothin' but tears.
