33.8: Ain't nobody out on the roads. Travelin' man shut down. The agreements? Broken. Cities? Disrespected. People? Don't even matter no more.
33.9: The whole land lookin' dry and tired. Lebanon embarrassed, Sharon dry like desert. Bashan and Carmel done dropped all they fruit.
33.10: "Now it's My time," says the Lord. "I'ma stand up. I'ma show y'all who I really am."
33.11: Y'all been breathin' in lies and schemin'— You gon' birth nothin' but ashes. Yo own words? They gon' set you on fire.
33.12: Folks gon' burn up like lime in a fire pit. Like dry thorns—they gone.
33.13: Listen up! Y'all far away—hear what I did. Y'all close by—respect My power.
33.14: Even Zion's sinners shook now. The fake ones tremblin', askin': "Who can survive God's heat? Who can stand in this everlasting blaze?"
33.15: Only the ones walkin' right, Talkin' truth, Not takin' dirty money, Not listenin' to violence, Not watchin' evil.
33.16: That one? He safe— Gon' live high up in a strong fortress. He won't lack nothin'—bread steady, water sure.
33.17: You gon' see the King in all His beauty. And the land ahead? It's wide and full of promise.
33.18: Your heart gon' think back like, "Man, remember when we was scared? Where them tax men at? Where the enemy countin' our defenses?"
33.19: You won't see them wild people no more— No more confusing tongues, no more threats you don't even understand.
33.20: Look at Zion, God's city of feasts. Your eyes gon' see Jerusalem— Peaceful, steady, can't be moved. A tent that don't collapse, With ropes and stakes that don't snap.
33.21: That's where God gon' be our everything— A river too wide for enemy ships. No boats creepin' in. No sneak attacks.
33.22: 'Cause the Lord is our Judge. The Lord writes the laws. The Lord is our King. He the one who gon' save us.
33.23: The enemy ships? Can't even raise their sails. Their ropes loose, their gear busted. And all that treasure they tried to hold? Even the folks who was limpin' gon' snatch it up.
33.24: And the people livin' there? Ain't nobody talkin' 'bout "I'm sick" no more— 'Cause they sins forgiven. They good now.

34.1: Yo, all y'all nations—come close and listen. Everybody on earth, pay attention. This message ain't just for some—it's for the whole world.
34.2: God mad. Not just a little upset—He full-on furious with every nation out here. He ain't sparin' nobody. He already decided—they done for.
34.3: Bodies gon' be everywhere, tossed out. The stench? It's gon' be awful. Mountains soaked in blood—like the land itself cryin'.
34.4: Even the skies gon' break down. The stars gon' fall like old leaves off a vine, Or like figs droppin' off a tree in the wind.
34.5: God said, "My sword done been sharpened in heaven, Now it's comin' for Edom— Them folks I done marked for destruction."
34.6: That sword? It's drippin' with blood, Soaked with fat from the offerings— Lambs, goats, rams— 'Cause God holdin' court in Bozrah, And the whole land of Edom gon' be a slaughterhouse.
34.7: Even the wild bulls gon' fall with the regular ones. Blood gon' flood the land, And the dirt gon' be greasy with fat.
34.8: Why? 'Cause this the day God finally settin' the record straight. Zion's pain ain't been forgotten. This the year God get payback for all the hurt they took.
34.9: Edom gon' be cursed land now. Rivers turn to black tar, Dust turn to burning sulfur. The whole joint gon' be on fire.
34.10: And it won't stop. That fire gon' burn day and night— Smoke risin' forever. Nobody livin' there again. No foot traffic.
34.11: Only creatures like pelicans, porcupines, owls, and ravens Gon' call it home now. God usin' a blueprint of chaos And bricks of emptiness to rebuild it— A whole redesign of destruction.
34.12: Ain't no royalty gon' be left. The princes? Gone. The throne? Empty. They ain't got no shot at comin' back.
34.13: Thorns takin' over palaces. Brambles where mansions used to be. Jackals movin' in. Ostriches takin' walks through what used to be fortresses.
34.14: Wild animals linkin' up—jackals and desert beasts chillin'. Goats callin' out to each other. Even night creatures settlin' in like, "Yeah, this our spot now."
34.15: Snakes layin' eggs, nesting, hatchin', Keepin' their babies in the shadows. Even hawks gon' post up there—each one findin' her match.
34.16: Look it up in the Book. Ain't none of this gon' miss. Every piece gon' fall in place—just like God said. His Spirit already called the roll and gave 'em the land.
34.17: God divvied it up Himself. Measured it with His own hand. Now it's theirs—forever. That land? Gon' stay cursed and inhabited by beasts for all generations.

35.1: That dry land? Yeah, even the wilderness gon' be hype for what's comin'. The desert gon' rejoice like it just got a fresh rain. It's gon' bloom like roses outta concrete.
35.2: Flowers poppin' up everywhere, joy bustin' out with songs. Lebanon's glory, Carmel's beauty, Sharon's shine— All that splendor gon' be right there. They gon' see the glory of the Lord, How excellent our God really is.
35.3: Tell the ones whose hands weak, Whose knees be shakin': "Stand tall. Hold ya head up."
35.4: Say to the ones scared deep down, "Don't trip. Don't be afraid. God comin' for real this time— And He not just showin' up, He bringin' vengeance. He comin' to settle all accounts. He gon' save y'all."
35.5: Then the blind? They gon' see. The deaf? Ears wide open.
35.6: Folks who couldn't walk? They gon' leap like deer. And folks who ain't had no voice? They gon' sing loud. 'Cause water gon' bust out in dry places, Rivers showin' up where the desert used to rule.
35.7: Cracked ground turnin' into swimming holes. Thirsty land overflowin' with springs. The same spots jackals used to prowl? Now it's grass, reeds, and fresh life.
35.8: And there's gon' be a road runnin' through it— Called the Highway of Holiness. No mess allowed on this road—no foulness, no foolishness. Even if you ain't the smartest one walkin' it, You won't get lost.
35.9: Ain't no lions prowlin'. No wild beasts lurkin'. Only the ones God redeemed walk this road.
35.10: God's people—the ones He paid for—they comin' home. Marchin' to Zion with songs in their mouths And forever-joy on they heads. They gon' be full of gladness, And sorrow? Gone. Sighin'? Outta there. Just joy. Nothing but joy.

36.1: In the 14th year of King Hezekiah's reign, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, rolled up on all Judah's fortified cities and straight took 'em.
36.2: Then he sent his mouthpiece—the Rabshakeh—from Lachish to Jerusalem, with a whole squad behind him. They posted up at the aqueduct near the road to Fuller's Field.
36.3: Eliakim (Hilkiah's son), Shebna the secretary, and Joah (Asaph's boy, the historian) stepped out to meet him.
36.4: The Rabshakeh started poppin' off: "Tell Hezekiah this—straight from the so-called 'great king,' the king of Assyria: Why y'all so confident? Who gassed y'all up?"
36.5: "Y'all talkin' like y'all got strategy and muscle for war—but it's just talk. Who you even trustin' to make you think you can step to us?"
36.6: "Oh, you leanin' on Egypt? That weak stick? That cracked cane? If you put weight on that, it's just gon' stab through your hand. That's Pharaoh for you—he'll let down anybody who leans on him."
36.7: "Now if you tryna say, 'We trust in the Lord our God,' Ain't Hezekiah the same dude who tore down His altars and high places, And told y'all to only worship at this one altar in Jerusalem?"
36.8: "I'll even give y'all 2,000 horses right now… If y'all got enough men to even ride them. (Spoiler: You don't.)"
36.9: "If you can't even take one of our lowest-ranking soldiers, What makes you think Egypt gon' come save you with chariots and riders?"
36.10: "And let me tell you this: You think I came here without the Lord? Nah. He told me Himself— 'Go up against this land and wreck it.'"
36.11: Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah stepped in like, "Yo, speak in Aramaic. We understand you. Don't talk Hebrew in front of these people on the wall."
36.12: Rabshakeh was like, "Man, y'all think this message is just for y'all? Nah. The folks sittin' on that wall— They the ones who gon' suffer, Eatin' their own waste and drinkin' their own piss with y'all."
36.13: Then he yelled even louder, talkin' Hebrew now: "Listen up, Jerusalem! Hear the word of the great king of Assyria!"
36.14: "Don't let Hezekiah lie to y'all! He can't save you. Period."
36.15: "Don't let him gas you with that 'God gon' save us' talk. This city ain't safe."
36.16: "Here's what my king says: Make peace with me. Bring me a gift. Come out now, and you can eat off your own vines and fig trees, Drink from your own wells."
36.17: "That is… until I take y'all to a new place— Just like this one, but better: Grain, wine, bread, vineyards… A sweet setup."
36.18: "But don't let Hezekiah play y'all, sayin', 'The Lord gon' deliver us.' Ain't none of the gods of the other nations saved their lands from me."
36.19: "Where the gods of Hamath and Arpad at? What about Sepharvaim? Did any of them stop me from takin' Samaria?"
36.20: "If all them gods couldn't stop me, Why y'all think the Lord gon' deliver Jerusalem?"
36.21: But the folks didn't say nothin'. Not a word. King Hezekiah had made it clear: "Don't respond to him."
36.22: So Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah tore their clothes in grief, Went back to Hezekiah, And told him everything Rabshakeh said.

37.1: When King Hezekiah heard what was goin' down, he tore his clothes, threw on some sackcloth, and went straight to God's house.
37.2: He sent Eliakim (his house manager), Shebna (the scribe), and the elders of the priests—all wearin' sackcloth too—to go holla at the prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz.
37.3: They told Isaiah, "This day right here is full of pain, shame, and disrespect. It's like a woman tryna give birth but she too weak to push.
37.4: Maybe the Lord your God gon' hear the trash the Rabshakeh talked—the stuff the king of Assyria sent him to say against the livin' God—and God gon' check him for it. So please pray for the folks who still hangin' on."
37.5: Hezekiah's people gave Isaiah the message.
37.6: Isaiah replied, "Tell Hezekiah this: God said, 'Don't be shook by what you heard. Those dudes talkin' reckless? I heard 'em.
37.7: I'ma stir the king of Assyria's spirit, make him hear somethin' that'll send him runnin' back home—and when he gets there, he gon' get taken out with the sword.' "
37.8: The Rabshakeh dipped and found his king fightin' at Libnah, since he had left Lachish.
37.9: Word came that Tirhakah, the king of Ethiopia, was comin' to fight him. So Sennacherib sent another message to Hezekiah:
37.10: "Don't let your God play you, talkin' about 'Jerusalem won't fall into my hands.'
37.11: You heard what I did to everybody else—wiped 'em out! You think you different?
37.12: Their gods ain't save them: Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, Eden in Telassar—gone!
37.13: What happened to the kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? Exactly."
37.14: Hezekiah took that letter, read it, and went back to God's house. He laid it out right there in front of the Lord.
37.16: "Lord of Heaven's armies, God of Israel, chillin' between the cherubim—you God all by Yourself. Ain't no other. You made heaven and earth.
37.17: Please listen, Lord. Look at this! Hear what Sennacherib said—he tryin' You, the livin' God!
37.18: Yeah, he really did wipe out them other nations, no cap.
37.19: And he threw their gods in the fire—but that's 'cause they weren't really gods! Just man-made—wood and stone. So of course they ain't save nobody.
37.20: But Lord, we different. Please save us, so everybody out there will know—You alone are God."
37.21: Isaiah sent word back: "Because you prayed, Hezekiah, here's what the Lord says:
37.22: Zion—God's daughter—laughin' at that clown. Jerusalem just shook her head like, 'Boy, bye.'
37.23: Who you really think you was talkin' to? You raised your voice at God. You mocked the Holy One of Israel.
37.24: You bragged about your army, said you was gon' climb mountains, chop down Lebanon's best trees, take over forests and springs.
37.25: You said you drank up rivers and stomped through defenses like it was nothin'.
37.26: But hold up—I planned all that long ago. You just fulfillin' My will. You was supposed to knock over cities—I let that happen.
37.27: Their folks were weak anyway, like dry grass or rooftop weeds. They ain't stand a chance.
37.28: But I know where you stay. I know when you move. I know you mad.
37.29: And since your rage came up in My face, I'ma put My hook in your nose, My bridle in your mouth, and send you right back the way you came."
37.30: "Here's your sign: This year, y'all gon' eat whatever grows on its own. Next year too. But the third year? Plant, reap, and enjoy.
37.31: And the ones left in Judah? They gon' take root and grow strong again."
37.32: "Out of Jerusalem, a remnant gon' rise. Outta Zion, survivors will step forward. The Lord's passion gon' make it happen."
37.33: "So here's the deal about that Assyrian king: He not even gon' step foot in this city. He won't shoot no arrows, Won't hold no shields up, Won't build no siege ramps.
37.34: He leavin' the same way he came. He not comin' in here," says the Lord.
37.35: "I'ma protect this city, not for y'all— But for Me and My servant David."
37.36: That night, the angel of the Lord showed up and wiped out 185,000 Assyrian soldiers. When folks woke up? Bodies everywhere.
37.37: So Sennacherib bounced back to Nineveh, tail tucked.
37.38: But while he was worshipin' his fake god Nisroch, two of his own sons—Adrammelech and Sharezer—shanked him. They ran off to Ararat. Then his son Esarhaddon took the throne.

38.1: Around that time, King Hezekiah got real sick—like, deathbed sick. The prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz, came to him and said, "God said: Get your affairs in order. You ain't gon' make it."
38.2: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and started prayin'.
38.3: He said, "Lord, please remember how I been walkin' with You for real—heart loyal, doin' right by You. Don't let it end like this." And the man broke down cryin', hard.
38.4: Then God spoke to Isaiah again,
38.5: "Go tell Hezekiah this: The Lord, the God of David your ancestor, heard your prayer. I saw them tears. I'm givin' you 15 more years.
38.6: And I'm not just savin' you—I'm gon' save this whole city from that Assyrian king. I got y'all covered."
38.7: "And to prove I'm serious, here's your sign:
38.8: I'ma make the sun move back 10 degrees on the sundial of Ahaz." And just like that, the sun backed it up ten degrees.
38.9: This is Hezekiah's own writing after God healed him:
38.10: "I said, In the middle of my life, I'm bout to die? I won't even get to live out my full years."
38.11: "I said, I won't get to see God While I'm alive on this earth. Won't get to see nobody no more, Won't be with the living."
38.12: "My life was snatched up Like somebody snatching down a tent. It's like I was a thread on a loom— Then God just cut it. From sunup to sundown, You was takin' me out."
38.13: "I laid there thinkin' all night, Like a lion tearin' up bones, You was breakin' me down, Lord."
38.14: "I was chirpin' like a bird, Mournin' like a dove, Eyes weak from lookin' up, Just cryin' out: 'Lord, I'm overwhelmed—please come through for me!'"
38.15: "What else could I even say? You told me what was gon' happen, And You did it. Now I'm tryna walk light— This shook me deep."
38.16: "But I learned somethin'— It's these hard things that teach us how to really live. You used this to save my life."
38.17: "Truth is, That pain brought me peace. You snatched me from the grave, And You threw my sins behind Your back."
38.18: "The grave can't thank You, Death don't worship You, Dead folks don't get to hope in Your promises."
38.19: "But the livin'? Oh, the livin' gon' praise You. That's what I'm doin right now. And I'ma make sure my kids know Your truth too."
38.20: "God came through for me, So we gon' sing with stringed instruments All our days in the house of the Lord!"
38.21: Isaiah had told them to press a fig poultice on Hezekiah's boil so he'd heal.
38.22: And Hezekiah had asked, "What sign will show me I'll be well enough to go back to the Lord's house?"

39.1: Around that time, Merodach-Baladan, son of Baladan and king of Babylon, heard Hezekiah was sick but bounced back. So he sent him letters and a gift.
39.2: Hezekiah was feelin' real good about that, so he went and showed off everything—his stash of silver, gold, spices, oils, his whole armory—all his treasures. Bruh showed them everything.
39.3: Then Isaiah the prophet came through like, "So what them men say to you? Where they from?" Hezekiah answered, "They came all the way from Babylon. Real far."
39.4: Isaiah followed up: "Aight, so what exactly did they see in your house?" Hezekiah was like, "Everything. I showed 'em the whole spot—didn't hide nothin'."
39.5: Then Isaiah hit him with a word from the Lord:
39.6: "Listen up. The time's comin' when everything in your house—all that your ancestors stacked up—gon' be taken to Babylon. Ain't nothin' gon' be left. That's the Lord talkin'."
39.7: "And even some of your sons, your descendants, gon' be taken too. They'll end up as eunuchs servin' in the king of Babylon's palace."
39.8: Hezekiah said, "Well… that word from the Lord is good." (He was thinkin', "At least things gon' stay peaceful and cool while I'm still alive.")

40.1: "Tell My people to chill and be comforted," says God.
40.2: "Let Jerusalem know it's over now. The war done. Her mess been forgiven. She took the hit—double for all that sin. But it's settled."
40.3: A voice cryin' out in the wilderness: "Get the road ready for the Lord! Make a path in this dry place—a highway for our God."
40.4: Every low place gon' rise up. Every mountain and hill gon' get brought down. Crooked roads straightened, rough paths smoothed out.
40.5: God's glory about to show out, and everybody gon' see it together—'cause the Lord Himself said it.
40.6: A voice said, "Cry out!" I asked, "What I'm supposed to say?" "All people? They like grass. Their beauty? Just like flowers in a field."
40.7: "Grass fades, flowers droop, when God breathes on 'em. Yep, people are just like that grass."
40.8: "Grass withers. Flowers fade. But God's Word? That thing stands forever."
40.9: Zion, you got good news—go shout it from the hills! Jerusalem, raise your voice! Don't be scared—yell it loud: "Check out your God!"
40.10: Look, the Lord is comin' strong, flexin' His power. He got His reward with Him, and His work right in front.
40.11: Like a shepherd, He gon' feed His people. He gon' scoop the babies up in His arms, holdin' them close, and gently guide the mamas with little ones.
40.12: Who you know that can cup the oceans in His palm? Who can stretch out the skies like He do? Weigh dust? Stack up mountains on a scale?
40.13: Who been God's advisor? Who gave Him game?
40.14: Who taught Him justice, knowledge, or understanding? Nobody.
40.15: The nations? Just a drop in the bucket. Some little specks on a scale. He lifts islands like they nothin'.
40.16: Even all of Lebanon's trees wouldn't make enough firewood for an offering worthy of Him.
40.17: To God, nations ain't even a blip. Less than nothin'. Straight-up empty.
40.18: So who you gon' compare to God? What could even come close?
40.19: Somebody tries to make a statue—gold-plated, silver-chained, real fancy.
40.20: And if you broke? You just pick a solid tree and find a skilled worker to carve you something that won't fall over.
40.21: Don't you know? Ain't you heard? Ain't this been known since day one? Since the foundation of the world?
40.22: God sits above the circle of the earth—folks look like grasshoppers from up there. He stretches out the skies like a curtain, like He settin' up a tent to live in.
40.23: He shuts down rulers like it's nothin'. Judges? Powerless before Him.
40.24: Before they even get rooted good, He breathes on 'em—they wither. Whirlwind snatchin' them up like dry weeds.
40.25: "Who y'all gon' compare Me to? Who stands on My level?" says the Holy One.
40.26: Look up! See all them stars? He made 'em. Calls 'em by name. Not one missing—'cause He that strong.
40.27: Why you trippin', Jacob? Why you think God forgot about you? Why you actin' like He ain't listenin' to your struggle?
40.28: You ain't heard? God ain't new to this—He the everlasting Creator. He don't get tired. He don't doze off. And His wisdom? Unsearchable.
40.29: He gives power to the ones who ain't got it. Strength to the ones runnin' on E.
40.30: Even the young folk gon' get tired, pass out, and fall behind.
40.31: But if you wait on the Lord? Oh, you get your strength back. You gon' soar like eagles, run and not pass out, walk and not fall behind.

41.1: "Aight y'all coastlands—be quiet and pay attention! Let folks get they strength up, step forward, and speak. Let's come face-to-face and settle this."
41.2: "Who raised up that one from the East? Called him with righteousness at his heels? Who handed nations over to him, made him boss up over kings? Who turned his enemies into dust under his sword, and dry weeds under his bow?"
41.3: "He chased 'em down, safe and smooth, takin' a road he ain't even been on before."
41.4: "Who been doin' all this from way back? Who been callin' generations like roll call?" "It's Me—the Lord! I'm the first, and I'm still here with the last."
41.5: The islands saw what went down and got shook. Folks from far off got scared, but came closer anyway.
41.6: Everybody hypin' each other up: 'Yo, stay strong, bruh!'
41.7: The metalworker boostin' the goldsmith. The hammer guy gassin' up the one who strikes the anvil, like, "It's ready now!" Then they nail it down so it don't fall over.
41.8: "But you, Israel? You My servant. Jacob, I chose you. You from Abraham—My homeboy."
41.9: "I pulled you from the ends of the earth, called you out from far away, and said: 'You Mine. I picked you. I ain't tossin' you away.'"
41.10: "So don't be scared—I'm with you. Don't trip—I'm your God. I'm gon' hold you up, strengthen you, help you out, and keep you steady with My righteous right hand."
41.11: "Anybody mad at you? Watch—shame and embarrassment. They gon' vanish like they never was. All your enemies? Gone."
41.12: "You gon' look around like, 'Where they at?' But you ain't findin' 'em. They disappeared like smoke in the wind."
41.13: "I'm the Lord, your God, holdin' your hand tight, tellin' you: 'Don't be scared. I got you.'"
41.14: "Don't fear, lil Jacob. Yeah, you feelin' like a worm out here. But I got you," says the Lord—"Your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel."
41.15: "I'm about to turn you into a brand-new threshing sledge—sharp and ready. You gon' crush mountains and stomp down hills like it's nothin'."
41.16: "You gon' throw all that junk in the air, and the wind gon' sweep it up. Whirlwinds gon' blow it away. Then you gon' rejoice in Me and give Me glory."
41.17: "Poor folks out here thirsty, mouths dry as dust—but I hear 'em. I ain't forgot. I'm the God of Israel. I got 'em."
41.18: "I'll bust rivers open on high hills, make fountains pop up in dry valleys. Turn deserts into pools, cracked ground into streams."
41.19: "I'm plantin' cedars, acacia, myrtle, olive trees—cypress, pine, boxwood too—all up in that dry land."
41.20: "So when folks see it, they gon' know—this ain't nature, this ain't luck—this was God. The Holy One of Israel did this."
41.21: "Go on then—bring your receipts," says the Lord. "Present your strongest case," says the King of Jacob.
41.22: "Show us what's comin'. Tell us the past too, break it down. Help us understand how it all ends. Speak on it."
41.23: "Tell us what's next. Show us you really gods. Do something! Good or bad, just make some noise so we know y'all exist."
41.24: "Y'all ain't nothin'. Your work? Trash. Anyone who picks you? Straight up bogus."
41.25: "I raised one up from the north—he comin'. From the east, callin' on My name. He gon' stomp on rulers like soft clay under a potter's foot."
41.26: "Anybody call this from the jump? Nah. Anybody speak on this before it happened? Nope. Y'all heard nothin'."
41.27: "I was the first to say to Zion, 'Look, they comin'!' And I sent good news to Jerusalem."
41.28: "I looked around, couldn't find nobody. No man. No counselor. No one could give Me answers."
41.29: "They all worthless. Their work is a joke. Their idols? Wind and straight-up confusion."

42.1: "Look here—My Servant, the One I hold down. My chosen one, the One I'm proud of. I done put My Spirit on Him. He gon' bring justice to the nations, even outside y'all little circle."
42.2: "He ain't gon' be loud in the streets, ain't tryna be seen or heard shoutin' everywhere."
42.3: "If somebody barely hangin' on, He ain't gon' break 'em. If their fire almost out, He ain't gon' snuff it. He gon' make sure justice stands for real."
42.4: "He ain't quitting, and He ain't gettin' discouraged till justice runs deep in this whole earth. Even the islands out there waitin' on His Word."
42.5: God, the One who made the heavens and stretched 'em like a sheet, the One who laid out the earth and gave folks breath and spirit, He said this:
42.6: "I called You with righteousness. I'm holdin' Your hand. I'm keepin' You, and I'm givin' You to the people as a promise, a light to the nations."
42.7: "You gon' open blind eyes, free folks locked up, and pull folks outta dark places and prison cells."
42.8: "I'm the Lord. That's My name. I ain't sharin' My glory with no one, and definitely not with no fake statues."
42.9: "Look, the old things already happened. I'm speakin' new things now. I'm tellin' y'all before they pop off."
42.10: Y'all better sing a new song to the Lord! All y'all from sea to sea, from coast to coast—lift that praise up!
42.11: Wilderness towns, folks from Kedar, folks chillin' in Sela—y'all too, shout from the mountain tops!
42.12: Let everybody give God His glory and let His name ring out across every coastline.
42.13: God movin' like a warrior now. His energy stirred up like a dude ready for battle. He shoutin' loud, not holdin' back—He takin' the W against all enemies.
42.14: "I been quiet for a long time—held My peace. But now? I'ma let it out like a woman in labor—pantin', gaspin'. It's go time."
42.15: "I'ma knock down mountains, dry up rivers, scorch the hills—strip it all bare. No green left."
42.16: "I'ma guide the blind down paths they ain't even know. Turn darkness into light for 'em. Make crooked roads smooth. I ain't leavin' 'em behind. I'm doin' this for real."
42.17: "But the folks worshippin' statues? They gon' be embarrassed—real bad. Talkin' bout 'These our gods.' Pssh. Shame."
42.18: "Yo—deaf folks, listen up. Blind folks, open ya eyes."
42.19: "Who more blind than My own servant? Who more deaf than My messenger? Who missin' it like the one I sent?"
42.20: "They lookin' at everything but not seein'. Listenin' but not hearin'. Useless!"
42.21: The Lord wanted to show off righteousness. That's why He made the Law big and important.
42.22: But these folks? Robbed, jacked, locked up in spiritual jail cells. Ain't nobody comin' to get 'em. Ain't nobody sayin' 'Run that back!' or 'Free them!'
42.23: "Anybody gon' actually listen? Anybody hear what's comin'?"
42.24: "Y'all wonderin' who let Israel get robbed? Who let Jacob get snatched up? It was Me—the Lord. Why? 'Cause they kept breakin' My commandments and refused to walk in My ways."
42.25: "So I let My anger fall. Let 'em feel the heat from war. They got burned up all around and still didn't get it. Didn't even take it to heart."

43.1: But now, the Lord—the One who made you, Jacob, who formed you, Israel—He say: "Don't be scared. I done paid for you. I called you out by name. You belong to Me."
43.2: "When you walk through deep water, I'm gon' be right there. When the river rise up, it won't drown you. When the fire comes, you ain't gon' get burned. Not even touched."
43.3: "I'm the Lord your God. The Holy One. Your Savior. I gave up Egypt, Ethiopia, and Seba just to get you back."
43.4: "You real precious to Me. I value you. I love you. I'll trade lives just to keep you safe."
43.5: "Don't be afraid—I'm with you. I'll bring your people from every direction—east, west, north, and south."
43.6: "I'll tell the north: 'Let 'em go!' And the south: 'Don't hold 'em back!' Bring My sons and daughters home, no matter how far they been scattered."
43.7: "Everybody called by My name, made by Me for My glory—I made them, formed them, shaped them. They Mine."
43.8: Bring out the blind—even if they got eyes. Bring out the deaf—even if they got ears.
43.9: Gather all the nations together. Let the people show what they know. Can anybody explain what's been goin' on? Let 'em testify—prove it's truth.
43.10: "Y'all are My witnesses," says the Lord, "and My chosen servant. I picked you so you could know Me, trust Me, understand I'm the One. Ain't no God before Me. Ain't gon' be none after."
43.11: "I, yes Me, I'm the Lord. And there ain't no other savior but Me."
43.12: "I told y'all what was comin'. I saved you. I spoke truth. Wasn't no foreign god doin' that. That's why y'all My witnesses—I'm God."
43.13: "Even before time was a thing—I been Me. Ain't nobody takin' nothin' out My hand. When I move, can't nobody undo it."
43.14: The Lord, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel says: "I'ma shut Babylon down for y'all. I'ma make them run scared—those proud Chaldeans cruisin' in they ships."
43.15: "I'm the Lord, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King."
43.16: I'm the One who made a way through the sea, Split the deep waters wide open.
43.17: I pulled down the chariots, the horses, the whole army. They laid down, ain't gettin' back up. Snuffed out like a candle in the wind.
43.18: "Stop dwellin' on what happened before. Quit livin' in the past."
43.19: "I'm doin' something new—can't you see it? I'm makin' a way in the wilderness, puttin' rivers where the desert been dry."
43.20: "Even the wild animals gon' praise Me—jackals, ostriches—'cause I'm givin' water in dry places, refreshin' My chosen people."
43.21: "This people? I made them for Me. And they gon' praise My name."
43.22: "But you, Jacob? You ain't been callin' on Me. You tired of Me, Israel."
43.23: "You ain't brought no offerings, no sacrifices. I ain't even ask for all that pressure."
43.24: "You ain't even bring Me no sweet incense. But you did bring Me all your sins. Heavy. You wearin' Me out."
43.25: "Still—I'm the One who wipes your sins away. Not 'cause you earned it, but 'cause I said so. I ain't gon' bring 'em back up either."
43.26: "Go ahead. Remind Me if you want. Bring your argument. Try and prove yourself."
43.27: "Your ancestors messed up. Even the ones supposed to speak for you been outta line."
43.28: "So I let your leaders fall, let the temple folks get cursed. Jacob been exposed. Israel been clowned."

44.1: Now listen up, Jacob—My servant. Israel—My chosen one.
44.2: This what the Lord say, the One who made you, formed you since you was in the womb, the One who got your back: "Don't be scared, Jacob My servant. Jeshurun, I picked you."
44.3: "I'ma pour water on the ones who thirsty. I'ma flood the dry land. I'ma pour out My Spirit on your kids, and bless all your babies."
44.4: "They gon' grow up like willows by the water, flourishing, thriving."
44.5: One gon' say, 'I belong to the Lord.' Another gon' call himself a child of Jacob. Somebody else gon' tattoo 'Property of the Lord' on they hand and rep Israel by name.
44.6: This what the Lord, Israel's King and Redeemer, the Lord of armies, gotta say: "I'm the First and the Last. Ain't nobody else God but Me."
44.7: "Who else can speak on the future like I do? If they real with it, let them say what's comin'. Let them line it up like I did from the jump."
44.8: "Don't be scared. I already told y'all what's up. Y'all My witnesses. Is there another God? Nah. Ain't no other Rock. I ain't heard of one."
44.9: Folks who make idols? All of 'em useless. What they value won't do nothin' for 'em. They witness their own mess. They blind and clueless.
44.10: Who in they right mind makes a god that don't even help them?
44.11: Even the crew around them gon' be embarrassed. These dudes just human. Let 'em all gather—they still gon' be shook and ashamed.
44.12: The blacksmith sweatin' in the fire, hammerin' with tired arms. But he get weak, don't eat, and pass out.
44.13: The woodworker drawin' lines, using chalk and rulers, carving it to look like a man. All that just to sit in the house like decor.
44.14: He cuts down trees—cedar, cypress, oak. He plants pine trees, waits for rain, then—
44.15: —uses the wood to warm up, bake bread… and also carves an idol to worship. Same wood. He bowin' down to it.
44.16: One half goes in the fire to roast meat, and he say, "Mmm, I'm full and warm."
44.17: Other half? He turn it into a god. Falls down to it like, "Save me, you my god now."
44.18: They don't even realize they lost. God let 'em stay blind. They can't see or understand.
44.19: Ain't nobody stoppin' to think: "Yo, I used this wood to cook dinner… now I'm worshipin' the leftovers?"
44.20: That man's just eatin' ashes—straight delusional. He too far gone to even ask, "Yo, is this a lie in my hand?"
44.21: "Remember this, Jacob. Israel—you My servant. I made you. You belong to Me. I ain't forgot you."
44.22: "I erased your mess-ups like clouds disappear. I wiped out your sin like morning mist. Come back to Me—I already paid the price."
44.23: Sing, heavens! Shout, earth! Let the mountains get loud! Trees, clap your hands! The Lord redeemed Jacob and flexed His glory through Israel.
44.24: This what the Lord say—your Redeemer, the One who formed you since the womb: "I'm the One who made everything. I spread out the sky, stretched out the earth—all by Myself."
44.25: "I shut down fake prophets. I drive fortune-tellers crazy. I flip the script on the 'wise' and make their wisdom dumb."
44.26: "But when My servants speak, I back it up. When My messengers move, I make it happen. I told Jerusalem: 'You gon' be lived in again.' I told Judah: 'Your cities gon' be rebuilt. The ruins? I'ma lift 'em.'"
44.27: "I told the sea, 'Dry up.' And it dried."
44.28: "And I got Cyrus lined up. He My shepherd. He gon' do what I want—sayin' to Jerusalem, 'You gon' be rebuilt,' and to the Temple, 'Your foundation gon' be laid.'"

45.1: This what the Lord say to His chosen one, Cyrus—the one He holdin' by the right hand: "I'ma help you take down nations, loosen kings' belts, and open doors no man can shut."
45.2: "I'ma walk in front of you and clear the path, flatten the bumps, bust open bronze gates, and cut through iron bars."
45.3: "I'ma give you treasure from the shadows, riches folks ain't even know was hid, so you know it's Me—the Lord—callin' your name, the God of Israel."
45.4: "For the sake of Jacob My servant, and Israel who I picked, I'm callin' you by name, even though you don't know Me like that."
45.5: "I'm the Lord, ain't no one else. Ain't no God besides Me. I'm the one dressin' you for the fight, even though you ain't never called on Me."
45.6: "So folks all over—east to west—know ain't nobody else but Me. I'm the Lord. That's it. Period."
45.7: "I make light. I create dark. I bring peace. I stir up trouble. I'm the Lord—I do all that."
45.8: "Heavens, open up and let justice rain down! Let the skies pour out what's right. Let the earth open up and grow salvation, let righteousness sprout up side by side. I, the Lord, planted it."
45.9: Woe to the one tryna argue with the One who made 'em. Like clay tryna clap back at the potter. "Yo, what you makin'?" Or sayin', "You ain't got no hands."
45.10: Or the fool tellin' his daddy, "Why you birth me?" Or his mama, "What you even bring me here for?"
45.11: This what the Lord—the Holy One of Israel—say: "You wanna ask Me what's next for My kids? Wanna question My plans with My own hands?"
45.12: "I made this earth. Created folks to live on it. Spread the heavens out with My own hands. Every star out there? I gave orders."
45.13: "I raised up Cyrus on the right path. I'll make sure he walk it right. He gon' rebuild My city. Let My people go free. No ransom. No bribes." That's what the Lord of armies said.
45.14: The Lord said: "Egypt's riches, Cush's goods, the tall folk from Seba—they gon' come to you. Chains on 'em. Bowing down. Sayin', 'God with you, for real. Ain't no other God.'"
45.15: For real, Lord, You stay movin' in silence. O God of Israel, our Savior!
45.16: Idol-makers? Embarrassed and confused. All of 'em gon' be shamed.
45.17: But Israel? The Lord got y'all. Saved forever. No shame. No disgrace. Ever again.
45.18: The Lord, Creator of heaven and earth—He made it, formed it, set it up to be lived in—He said: "I'm the Lord. Ain't no one else."
45.19: "I ain't whisper in some shadow corner. I ain't tell Jacob, 'Seek Me' for nothin'. I speak truth. I say what's right."
45.20: Gather up, y'all who escaped from the nations. Them other folks? Still carryin' wooden statues. Still prayin' to gods that can't even save 'em.
45.21: Let 'em come with their best argument. Bring they facts. Who called this from the beginning? Who told it way back then? Ain't it Me—the Lord? Ain't no other God out there. Just Me. The Just One. The Savior.
45.22: "Look to Me and be saved, all y'all—from the far ends of the earth. I'm God. Ain't no one else."
45.23: "I swore by Myself, and I don't take it back—every knee gon' bow to Me. Every tongue gon' confess."
45.24: They gon' say, 'Only in the Lord is righteousness and strength.' People gon' come to Him. But everybody beefin' with Him? They gon' be embarrassed.
45.25: But in the Lord, the whole fam of Israel gon' be made right. And they gon' shine in His glory.

46.1: Bel done bowed down. Nebo bent over. Them so-called gods sittin' heavy on oxen and cattle—they ain't helpin' nobody. They just extra weight.
46.2: Both them idols crouched down together. They couldn't save nobody. They couldn't even save themselves from bein' dragged off into exile.
46.3: "Listen up, house of Jacob, all y'all still left in Israel—I been holdin' you down since birth, carried you straight out the womb."
46.4: "Even when you get old and gray, I'm still gon' be Him. Still carryin' you. I made you. I got you. I'll keep carryin' you. I'll rescue you."
46.5: "So tell Me this—Who y'all gon' compare Me to? Who y'all put next to Me like we the same?"
46.6: "Y'all tossin' gold out your bags, weighin' silver out, hiring somebody to shape it into a so-called god—then bowin' down like it did somethin'."
46.7: "You gotta lift it up yourself, carry it, set it in place—and it don't even move. You cry out to it, and it just sit there. It can't talk. It can't help. It can't save."
46.8: "Y'all need to think back. Man up. Wake up, y'all rebellious folks."
46.9: "Remember what I already did. I'm God—ain't nobody else. I'm God—and ain't nobody like Me."
46.10: "I be callin' the end from the beginning, talkin' about stuff before it even pop off. Whatever I say gon' happen, period. What I want? It's gettin' done."
46.11: "I'll call a wild bird out the east, a man from far away to do what I planned. I said it. I meant it. It's gon' happen."
46.12: "Y'all hardheaded ones, who still far from livin' right—listen."
46.13: "My righteousness comin' close. It ain't far. My salvation ain't holdin' back. I'm settin' up deliverance in Zion, and Israel gon' shine in My glory."

47.1: Come down and sit in that dust, Babylon. You ain't sittin' on no throne now, princess. Go ahead and sit on the ground, Chaldean girl—ain't nobody callin' you soft and fancy no more.
47.2: Pick up them millstones, grind some flour. Take off that veil. Roll up that skirt. Get them legs in the river. You walkin' now.
47.3: Yo nakedness gon' be out here, Yo shame gon' be front and center. I'm takin' vengeance. Ain't no negotiations.
47.4: (Our Redeemer—He the Lord of Armies. That's His name. The Holy One of Israel.)
47.5: Sit down and shut up. Fade into the shadows, Chaldean daughter. You ain't "The Lady of Kingdoms" no more.
47.6: I was mad at My people, So I let you handle 'em for a minute—But you took it too far. You ain't show no mercy, Not even to the old folks. You went hard.
47.7: You got cocky. Said, "I'm gon' be queen forever." You ain't think about consequences. You ain't plan for the end.
47.8: So now, hear this—You who livin' lavish, all comfy in yo bubble, Sayin' in your heart, "Ain't nobody like me. I'll never be a widow or lose my kids."
47.9: Guess what? Both them things comin' for you. And not next year—same day. Loss gon' hit you full force. Why? All them spells, All them rituals you been playin' with.
47.10: You been leanin' on yo evil ways, Tellin' yourself, "Ain't nobody watchin'." You got smart with it—too smart. But your wisdom twisted you up. You steady tellin' yourself, "I'm that girl. Ain't nobody else."
47.11: But evil comin'—and you won't even see it comin'. Disaster gon' hit—And you won't know how to dodge it. Ruin gon' fall in your lap, And you won't be ready.
47.12: Go ahead. Try them spells again. All them tricks you been doin' since you was young. Maybe they'll work this time. Maybe.
47.13: You tired from tryin' everything under the sun. Call them astrologers. Call them stargazers. Call them folks readin' the moon. Tell 'em to save you—We'll wait.
47.14: They gon' burn like straw. That fire gon' eat them up. They can't even save themselves, Let alone you. That fire ain't for warmin' hands. Ain't no cozy firepit—it's destruction.
47.15: That's how it's gon' be for all them folks you been rockin' with since way back. Your merchants? Gone. Everybody gon' dip to their corner, And you? Ain't nobody comin' to save you.

48.1: Listen up, house of Jacob—Y'all who say y'all reppin' Israel, Who claim you from Judah's roots, Swearin' by the Lord's name, Droppin' God's name like you livin' right—But you not real with it.
48.2: You act like you part of the holy city, You lean on the name of the God of Israel, But let's be real—The Lord of Armies ain't fooled.
48.3: I told y'all what was gon' happen way back. I said it, then I made it pop off. I ain't waste no time.
48.4: I knew y'all hardheaded. Stiff-necked like you got iron in your spine. Forehead hard like bronze.
48.5: That's why I told you before it happened—So you wouldn't turn around and say, "My little idol did that." Nah. That was Me.
48.6: You heard all this—So what you gon' say now? I'm droppin' new stuff on you now, Fresh revelations you ain't never heard before.
48.7: It's brand new, not recycled. I ain't give it to you before, So don't act like, "Oh yeah, I already knew that."
48.8: No you didn't. Your ears been shut. You ain't been listenin'. I already knew you were shady—Been wildin' since the womb.
48.9: But for the sake of My name, I'm holdin' back My anger. For My own glory, I'm not cuttin' y'all off just yet.
48.10: I've been refin' you—Not like silver in a clean shop, But like throwin' you into fire—Hard times been shapin' you.
48.11: I'm doin' this for Me. Ain't gon' let My name get played. I don't share My shine with nobody else.
48.12: Listen, Jacob. Listen, Israel—My chosen one: I'm Him. The First. The Last. Still here.
48.13: My hand built this whole planet, Stretched out the sky with My right hand. When I call, they stand up and salute.
48.14: Y'all, come together and hear this—Ain't nobody else told you this before. The Lord got love for this one I raised up. He gon' wreck Babylon And bring down the Chaldeans.
48.15: I called him. I brought him. And he gon' succeed 'cause I said so.
48.16: Get close. Hear Me clear: I ain't been speakin' in secret. Since day one, I been here. And now, the Lord God and His Spirit sent Me.
48.17: This what your Redeemer says—The Holy One of Israel: "I'm the Lord your God, Teachin' you how to win, Guidin' you in the right direction."
48.18: If only you had listened… Your peace would be flowin' like a river, Your righteousness rollin' like ocean waves.
48.19: Your descendants would've been like sand on the beach, Uncountable blessings. No one would've erased your name from My presence.
48.20: Get outta Babylon! Dip from the Chaldeans! Sing about it loud! Shout it 'til the ends of the earth: "The Lord came through for Jacob!"
48.21: When He led 'em through dry places, They ain't go thirsty. He cracked rocks and made water pour out. Straight up miracle moves.
48.22: But for the wicked? Ain't no peace for them. That's on God.

49.1: Listen up, y'all on the coasts. You folks far off—pay attention. God been had Me marked from the womb, Called My name while I was still in my mama's belly.
49.2: He made My mouth sharp like a sword, But kept Me tucked under His hand. Polished Me like a fine arrow—Then placed Me in His quiver for the right moment.
49.3: He said to Me, "You My Servant, Israel. I'm gon' shine through you."
49.4: But I said, "Man, I been grindin' for nothin'. All this work feel wasted. Still, My reward is safe with the Lord. My purpose? God still got that handled."
49.5: Now the Lord—the one who shaped Me from the womb—He speakin': He made Me to bring Jacob back, To gather Israel close again. And even if they don't see it yet, God sees Me, and He say I'm glorious. He My strength.
49.6: And He said, "Just bringin' Israel back? That ain't even enough. I'm sendin' You as a light to the nations, So My salvation can reach all the way to the ends of the earth."
49.7: The Lord, Israel's Redeemer, The Holy One—the One people been disrespectin'—Says this to the One they wrote off: Kings gon' stand up when they see You. Even princes gon' bow down. Why? 'Cause God ain't never been fake. He picked You.
49.8: The Lord says, "When the time was right, I heard You. On the day of salvation, I showed up. I'm gon' hold You down, Make You the covenant, Restore what's broken, And give back what looked lost.
49.9: You gon' tell the locked-up ones, 'You free now.' And those in the dark, 'Step into the light.' They'll eat even along empty roads, Find green in high places.
49.10: No more hunger. No thirst. No sun blazin' down on them. I'm gon' lead 'em gently, Take 'em to springs of water like a good shepherd.
49.11: Every mountain that was in the way? I'll turn it into a road. My highways? They'll rise above it all.
49.12: Look—they comin' from everywhere: North, west, even far-off lands like Sinim."
49.13: Rejoice, heavens! Earth, go 'head and sing! Mountains, lift up your voice! 'Cause the Lord comforted His people—And He ain't forgot the ones hurtin'.
49.14: But Zion was like, "God forgot about me." "He done left me."
49.15: But God said: "Can a mama forget the baby she nursed? Even if she did, I ain't forget you.
49.16: Look—I got your name tatted on My hands. Your walls? I'm watchin' them constantly.
49.17: Your kids comin' back fast, And the ones who tore you down? They leavin'.
49.18: Open your eyes and look around! All of them comin' home to you. As sure as I live," says the Lord, "You gon' wear them like jewelry—Like a bride dressin' up."
49.19: All that ruined land you thought was too empty? Now it's gon' be too small to hold all your people. The ones who crushed you? Nowhere in sight.
49.20: Your new children gon' say, "This spot too tight—we need more room!"
49.21: And you gon' say, "Where all these kids come from? I lost everything. I was exiled, alone, abandoned. Who raised these? I ain't even know they existed."
49.22: The Lord God says: "I'ma raise My hand and send a signal to the nations. They gon' bring your sons in their arms, Carry your daughters on their shoulders.
49.23: Kings gon' serve you like foster daddies. Queens gon' nurse your babies. They'll bow to you face-down, And lick the dust off your feet. Then you'll know—I'm the Lord. And the ones who wait on Me? They won't ever be disappointed."
49.24: Can the strong be robbed of what they hold? Can prisoners just walk free from the powerful?
49.25: But the Lord says, "Yes, even the mighty gon' lose their grip. I'm takin' back what's Mine. I'll fight the ones fightin' you. And I'ma save your babies."
49.26: Your oppressors gon' eat their own lies and defeat. They gon' drown in their own mess. And everybody gon' know—I, the Lord, am your Savior, Your Redeemer, The Mighty One of Jacob.

50.1: The Lord said: "So where that divorce paper at? The one sayin' I left y'all mama? Or who I owe money to that made Me sell y'all off? Truth is—it was your own sin that sold you out. Your wrongdoings the reason your mama got put away."
50.2: "When I came knockin', why nobody answered? When I called, why y'all act like you ain't hear Me? You think My arm too short to save you? You think I ain't got power? Look—I snap and dry up oceans. I shut rivers down 'til they turn to dust. Fish rotin' out here 'cause there ain't no water. That's Me."
50.3: "I throw black over the sky like it's cloth, I wrap the heavens in mourning like it's sackcloth."
50.4: "God gave Me a tongue that knows what's up, So I can drop a word right when somebody need it most. He wakes Me up every morning, Opens My ears like a student ready to learn."
50.5: "The Lord opened My ears—And I ain't fight it. I ain't dip out or run."
50.6: "I let folks beat My back. They snatched out My beard. They spit on Me. But I ain't cover My face or flinch."
50.7: "Why? 'Cause the Lord got Me. I ain't gon' be embarrassed. My face set like stone. I know I ain't gon' end up lookin' foolish."
50.8: "God right by Me—He the one who call Me right. So who tryna argue? Let's go—stand next to Me then. Who hatin'? Step up."
50.9: "The Lord gon' help Me. Ain't nobody else got the right to cancel Me. Them haters? They gon' fade like old clothes. Moths gon' eat 'em up."
50.10: "Who out here really reverences God? Who out here really listens to His Servant? If you walkin' in the dark, no light in sight—Don't quit. Trust in the name of the Lord. Lean on your God."
50.11: "But hey—You out here tryna light your own fires? Runnin' around with your own little sparks? Go 'head then—walk in your own glow. But here's what you gon' get from Me: You gon' lie down in pain."

51.1: Listen up, y'all who chasin' after what's right, Y'all who really tryna seek the Lord—Look back to where you came from. The rock that birthed you. The pit you was pulled up outta.
51.2: Think 'bout Abraham—your pops. And Sarah, the one who brought y'all forth. God called him when he ain't have nobody, Then turned around and blessed him heavy.
51.3: The Lord gon' comfort Zion for real. He gon' show up in all them dry, busted spots. That wilderness? It's gon' feel like Eden. The desert? Like God's own garden. Joy and laughter gon' echo through that place. Thanksgiving and music everywhere.
51.4: "Listen up, My people—Tune in, y'all who carry My name. My justice 'bout to go global, A light that everybody gon' see."
51.5: "I'm comin' through with righteousness. Salvation already on the move. My arms gon' handle these nations. And folks way out on them coastlands? They waitin' on Me. They trustin' in Me."
51.6: "Lift your eyes up. Look to the skies. Then peep the ground under your feet. This world? It gon' fade like smoke. People gon' drop like old clothes. But My salvation? It's eternal. My righteousness don't get canceled."
51.7: "If you really know what's right, If My Word live in your heart—Don't be scared of people's side-eyes. Don't flinch at they disrespect."
51.8: "They just fabric—moths eat fabric. But My righteousness? That's forever. My salvation? That's for generations on generations."
51.9: Wake up, Lord! Throw on Your strength like a fit! Just like You did back in the day. Ain't You the same One who shut Rahab down, And took out that sea serpent?
51.10: Ain't You the one who split the sea open So Your people could cross through it on dry land?
51.11: Them ones You saved gon' come home singin', They'll roll up to Zion with joy that don't expire. Sorrow? Gone. Tears? Gone. Only gladness gon' remain.
51.12: "It's Me—it's really Me—who comforts you. So why you so shook over another human, Somebody who gon' die just like grass? Why you forgot who made the sky and laid the Earth? You been scared every day, Worried about some oppressor."
51.13: "But where that oppressor now? Where all that rage they had?"
51.14: The one who been locked up? They 'bout to be free. They ain't gon' die in no hole. They gon' eat, live, and walk out.
51.15: "I'm the Lord your God. I cracked open that sea. I run the waves. That's Me—The Lord of Armies."
51.16: "I gave you My Word—put it in your mouth. Covered you with My hand for protection. Why? So I could replant the heavens, Lay the foundation again, And tell Zion, 'You My people.'"
51.17: Wake up! Get up, Jerusalem! You been sippin' straight from God's fury. You drank the whole cup—every bitter drop.
51.18: Ain't nobody left to guide you. None of your sons reachin' out for you. They all out here, but can't help.
51.19: Two things hit you hard: Destruction and famine. Sword and desolation. Who got the comfort for that?
51.20: Your sons out cold in the streets, Like deer caught in a trap. They full of the Lord's anger—That divine rebuke hit heavy.
51.21: So please, hear this now, You who been through it. You who feel drunk—but it ain't wine.
51.22: God's sayin'—"I'm your Lord. Your God. I fight for you. I'm takin' that cup of pain out your hand. You ain't gon' sip from My wrath no more."
51.23: "But the ones who walked on you? The ones who told you to lay down So they could step over you? They gettin' that cup now. You ain't the sidewalk no more."

52.1: Wake up, wake up, Zion! Throw on your strength like armor! Put on somethin' beautiful, Jerusalem, God's holy city ain't for the unclean no more—They ain't got access no more.
52.2: Dust yourself off. Rise up! Sit like a queen, Jerusalem. Break off them chains from your neck, You God's daughter—ain't no slave no more.
52.3: This what God say: "Y'all gave yourselves away for free, But I'm 'bout to buy y'all back—and it ain't costin' no cash."
52.4: God speakin': "My people went down to Egypt back in the day, Just tryna live. Then Assyria came outta nowhere, Oppressin' without reason."
52.5: "So now what's this I'm seein'? My people just bein' taken, no payment, no cause. These rulers got 'em cryin', And folks out here disrespectin' My name every day."
52.6: "But trust—My people gon' know My name. When that day hit, they gon' know for sure: 'I'm the One. I said it. I showed up.'"
52.7: How beautiful it is—Them feet comin' over the hills Bringin' good news. Talkin' peace. Spreadin' joy. Proclaimin' salvation. Tellin' Zion: "Yo God in charge!"
52.8: The watchmen gon' be singin' loud, All in sync—same voice. They gon' see the Lord do His thing And bring Zion back.
52.9: So let them ruins turn up—Sing out, Jerusalem! God done comforted His people, He done pulled up to redeem the city.
52.10: God done rolled up His sleeve, Showed the whole world He mean business. Every nation—every end of the Earth—Gon' witness the salvation of our God.
52.11: Go on, get outta there! Don't touch none of that dirty stuff. Y'all carrying the Lord's holy things—Be clean when you walk out.
52.12: And don't be runnin' like somebody scared. Ain't no panic. God got you. He up front, leadin' the way. And He got your back too—The God of Israel your rear guard.
52.13: "Look now—My Servant gon' move with wisdom. He gon' be lifted up, honored, praised."
52.14: Folks was shook when they saw Him—He ain't even look like a regular man. What He went through disfigured Him. He carried it all.
52.15: But He gon' sprinkle the nations—Bringin' cleansing. Even kings gon' shut up in awe. What they ain't never heard, they 'bout to see. What they ain't never imagined, it gon' hit them hard.

53.1: Who even gon' believe this right here? Who really seein' the strength of the Lord showin' up?
53.2: He came up like a young shoot, Like somethin' tryin' to grow outta dry ground. Ain't nothin' about Him that turned heads—No swag, no looks that made folks wanna choose Him.
53.3: He got hated on and pushed to the side, A man who knew pain like it was his roommate. We ain't even wanna look His way. He got disrespected, and we didn't think nothin' of Him.
53.4: But real talk? He carried our pain. He held our sadness on His back. But we thought He was bein' punished by God, Like He had it comin'.
53.5: Nah—He was hurt 'cause of our mess. He got bruised for the junk we did. He took the beatin' that made peace possible for us. And by His wounds, we got healed.
53.6: We all strayed off like lost sheep, Every single one of us doin' our own thing. But God dropped the weight of all our wrongs Right on Him.
53.7: He got mistreated, but He ain't say nothin'. Didn't even open His mouth. Like a lamb bein' walked to the butcher—Silent. Like a sheep gettin' shaved—Still didn't say a word.
53.8: They snatched Him up, locked Him down, passed judgment. Ain't nobody stood up for Him. They ended His life before it really started. He got struck down for what we did wrong.
53.9: They buried Him like a criminal—But He ended up restin' with the rich. Why? 'Cause He never did nobody dirty. Ain't no lies ever come out His mouth.
53.10: And somehow, God let it happen. He let Him go through it all. He offered His life for sin—But He gon' see His people, He gon' live on, And God's plan gon' win through Him.
53.11: After all that pain, He gon' look back and be satisfied. 'Cause through Him, many gon' be made right—All 'cause He carried the weight of their sins.
53.12: So now He gon' get a piece with the greats, Gon' share the victory with the strong—'Cause He gave His all, Took that death, Stood with the guilty, Carried the sin of many, And spoke up for the ones who didn't deserve it.

54.1: Go 'head and sing, sis—even if you ain't had no kids! Shout loud like you just gave birth, 'Cause the ones who felt left out Gon' have more than the ones who had it all together. That's what the Lord said.
54.2: Make room, baby! Stretch out your tent, Don't hold back. Add some square footage, Reinforce yo' stakes.
54.3: 'Cause you gon' spread out on both sides. Your people gon' take over nations, And them empty cities? You gon' fill 'em up.
54.4: Don't be scared—ain't no shame in your story no more. Forget the old wounds, Let go of the pain from your past, God ain't bringin' that back up.
54.5: Your Maker is now your man—The Lord of Heaven's Armies got you. Your Redeemer? The Holy One of Israel. He runnin' the whole earth.
54.6: God called you back like a husband callin' his young wife After leavin' her for a second, Feelin' her heartbreak.
54.7: I might've stepped back for a quick minute, But My mercy? That thing comin' in waves.
54.8: Yeah, I hid My face for a second in anger, But My love? That's gon' last forever. I'm comin' back for you with grace.
54.9: Just like I swore to Noah That the flood wouldn't hit again—I'm swearin' now I ain't gon' stay mad at you Or keep checkin' you.
54.10: Mountains might crumble, Hills might disappear, But My love ain't leavin' you. That peace I promised? Still locked in. That's on God.
54.11: You been hurt, tossed around, feelin' left out—But watch Me flip it. I'm gon' build you up with gems, Lay your foundation with sapphires.
54.12: Your towers gon' shine with rubies, Gates gon' sparkle like crystal, Every wall? Priceless.
54.13: And your babies? They gon' learn straight from the Lord. Peace? Overflowin'.
54.14: You gon' be rooted in righteousness. Oppression can't touch you. Fear? Nah. Terror? It can't even reach you.
54.15: Folks might try to come for you—But I ain't send 'em. And when they do? They gon' fall tryin'.
54.16: I made the blacksmith who blows them flames And creates weapons. I even made the one who tries to destroy.
54.17: But listen: No weapon formed against you gon' win. Any tongue tryna drag your name in court? You gon' shut it down. That's your inheritance as My servant. And your righteousness? Straight from Me. That's what the Lord said.

55.1: Aye! If you thirsty, come get some water. You broke? No problem—come eat anyway. Grab some wine and milk—no cash needed, no price tag attached.
55.2: Why you spendin' your money on junk that don't feed you? Why work so hard for stuff that don't satisfy? Listen up—eat what's good, And let your soul feast on real abundance.
55.3: Lean in, fam. Come close and really hear Me. Your soul gon' live, for real. I'm signin' an eternal deal with you—The same faithful love I showed David.
55.4: I made him a witness to the people, A true leader and commander in charge.
55.5: And guess what? You gon' call nations you don't even know, And folks who never heard of you? They gon' come runnin'. Why? 'Cause the Lord your God made you shine. The Holy One of Israel got you lookin' glorified.
55.6: Find the Lord while He's near. Call Him up before the line go dead.
55.7: Let the wicked man drop his ways, Let the shady one drop them thoughts. Come back to the Lord—He got mercy. Come back to our God—He forgives heavy.
55.8: "Look," says the Lord, "My thoughts ain't your thoughts, And My ways? They on a whole 'nother level.
55.9: Just like the sky higher than the ground, My ways higher than yours, And My thoughts? Way past yours."
55.10: Just like rain and snow come down from heaven, Waterin' the earth, Bringin' up fruit, feedin' the grower and the eater—
55.11: That's how My Word work. When I send it out, it don't come back empty. It's gon' do exactly what I wanted And prosper in the mission I sent it on.
55.12: You gon' leave with joy, And be led in peace. Even the mountains and hills gon' sing when they see you, And the trees out here? They clappin' for you like it's a standing ovation.
55.13: Instead of thorn bushes, cypress trees pop up. Instead of briers, myrtles grow. All this gon' be for the Lord's name—An eternal sign that won't ever be erased.

56.1: The Lord say: "Keep it just. Do what's right. My salvation comin' soon, And My righteousness 'bout to show up for real."
56.2: Blessed is the one who lives like this—Who hold tight to it, Don't break the Sabbath, And keep they hands clean from evil.
56.3: Don't let the foreigner who rolled with the Lord say, "God done pushed me out His circle." And don't let no eunuch say, "I'm washed up like a dead tree."
56.4: Nah, God say: To them eunuchs that hold down the Sabbath, Choose what pleases Me, And hold tight to My covenant—
56.5: I'ma give them a spot in My house, A name on My wall better than sons or daughters. An everlasting name that nobody can erase.
56.6: Same with the foreigners who ride for Me, Who serve Me and love My name, Who live like they belong to Me, Who keep the Sabbath and don't mess it up, And stick with My covenant—
56.7: I'ma bring them to My holy mountain. I'ma make 'em feel joy in My house of prayer. Their offerings? I'ma accept 'em. 'Cause My house? It's a house of prayer—for all nations.
56.8: The Lord God—the One who gathers all the outcasts of Israel—He say: "And I ain't done. I'ma gather even more to what's already been gathered."
56.9: All you wild beasts out there—come eat. You too, beasts of the forest—come feast.
56.10: The so-called watchmen? Blind as bats. Don't know nothin'. Can't speak up—just quiet like mute dogs. Laid out, sleepin' heavy, lovin' the nap life.
56.11: And they greedy too—like dogs that never get full. These "shepherds" don't understand the flock. They just out for self, Tryna get theirs from their own corners.
56.12: They say, "Come on, pour up the wine. Let's get lit. Tomorrow? It's gon' be just like today—Maybe even better."

57.1: The righteous folks die, And nobody really even cares. The kind-hearted get taken out, But ain't nobody askin' why—God spared 'em from the evil that was comin'.
57.2: They rest now, in peace. They lay down, Still walkin' in integrity, even in death.
57.3: But as for y'all? Come here, you sons of the sorceress, Children of adultery and scandal!
57.4: Who you out here clownin'? Who you makin' faces at, stickin' out your tongue? Ain't you the ones born in sin, Full of lies since day one?
57.5: You was wild under every green tree, Burnin' for them fake gods. Even sacrificed children in the valleys, Down in the shadows of the rocks.
57.6: You made them smooth river stones your gods. You poured drinks to 'em, brought grain offerings. You really think I'm cool with that?
57.7: Up high on the mountains, You laid out your bed—Went up there just to worship somethin' else.
57.8: Behind closed doors and secret spots, You stashed your idols. You opened yourself up to other lovers, Built bigger beds for 'em, Made shady deals and got comfortable in they beds, Lookin' at all that mess with lust in your eyes.
57.9: You chased after kings with perfumes and oils. You sent messages far away, Even down to the grave itself (Sheol). Chasin' every thrill.
57.10: You ran yourself ragged. But you ain't never say, "This ain't it." You kept chasin' what your hands could grab, So you ain't feel no remorse.
57.11: Who had you so shook That you had to lie? You forgot Me. Didn't even put Me in your heart. Was it 'cause I stayed quiet for a minute? That's why you stopped fearing Me?
57.12: I'ma call out your so-called righteousness And them deeds you brag on—They ain't gon' help you at all.
57.13: When you cry out, Let them idols you collected come save you. But the wind gon' blow them all away. Poof—gone. But whoever trusts Me? He gon' inherit the land. He gon' live on My holy mountain.
57.14: Somebody gon' say, "Clear the road! Move the mess out the way! Make room for God's people to walk free."
57.15: 'Cause the High and Holy One—the Eternal One—says: "I live way up in holiness, But I'm also close to the ones who feel low, The ones who know they need Me. I'm here to revive the brokenhearted, To breathe life into the humble."
57.16: I ain't gon' stay mad forever. I ain't gon' keep beef goin'. Y'all couldn't even survive if I did.
57.17: I was mad when y'all got greedy. I struck y'all down, hid My face. But y'all kept actin' up, Still runnin' with a hard heart.
57.18: But I seen it. And still—I'ma heal you. I'ma guide you. Bring comfort back to you and those who mourned with you.
57.19: I'ma speak peace into existence: "Peace, peace"—to the ones far and near. I will heal them, says the Lord.
57.20: But the wicked? They like a restless, raging sea—Can't chill. Just throwin' up dirt and mess everywhere.
57.21: Ain't no peace for the wicked. That's what my God said.

58.1: Shout it out loud! Don't hold back. Lift your voice like a trumpet—Tell My people what they doin' wrong, Call out Jacob's house on their mess.
58.2: They be actin' like they seek Me every day, Like they really want to know what I'm about. Like they some holy nation that stays righteous, And ain't turn they back on My commands. They ask Me for "justice," Actin' like they love to be in My presence.
58.3: "Why we fastin' and You ain't seein'? Why we afflictin' ourselves and You ain't payin' attention?" But check it—On the same day y'all fastin', Y'all still out here doin' whatever you want, Treatin' your workers dirty.
58.4: Y'all fastin' to start drama, Arguin' and fightin'—throwin' punches in the name of God. That ain't the kinda fast that's gon' move heaven.
58.5: You think I asked for that? Just for y'all to be lookin' sad, Head down, ashes on your face, Makin' a public show? That's what you call a fast? That's what you think I want?
58.6: This the fast I chose: Break the chains of injustice, Untie the heavy burdens, Free the oppressed, Tear down every yoke holdin' folks back.
58.7: Share your food with the hungry. Open your doors to the homeless. Give clothes to the ones out here naked. Don't act like you don't see your own people strugglin'.
58.8: Then—yeah, then—Your light gon' shine like the sunrise. Your healing? It gon' pop off fast. Your righteousness gon' be out front, And God's glory? It'll have your back.
58.9: Then when you call out, God gon' say, "Here I am." But you gotta stop with the heavy yokes, Stop pointin' fingers, And cut out all the hateful talk.
58.10: If you really look out for the hungry, If you care about the ones in pain—Then your light gon' break through the darkness, And even your night gon' feel like noon.
58.11: The Lord will keep guidin' you, Fillin' you up even in dry times, Strengthenin' your bones. You gon' be like a garden that stay green, Like a never-dry spring.
58.12: Your people gon' rebuild what was left in ruins. You gon' lay down legacy foundations. You'll be called "The Fixer of the Broken Walls," "The One Who Brought the Neighborhood Back."
58.13: If you stop wildin' on the Sabbath, And quit doin' your thing on My day—If you treat it like the gift it is, Holy and worthy, And stop speakin' on what you want…
58.14: Then you gon' be full of joy in the Lord. I'll lift you up to ride high on the land, And feed you from the inheritance I gave Jacob. The Lord Himself said that. No cap.

59.1: Look, God ain't too weak to save you. His hand still strong. His ears ain't clogged up either—He can hear you just fine.
59.2: The problem ain't with Him, it's with y'all. Your sins the ones buildin' a wall between you and God. Your mess done made Him turn His face away, So He ain't listenin' right now.
59.3: Your hands drippin' with blood, Your fingers dirty with wrongdoing. Your lips? Full of lies. And your tongue? Straight twisted.
59.4: Ain't nobody standin' up for what's right. Ain't nobody speakin' truth with their chest. They lean on lies, Plan evil, And birth nothin' but trouble.
59.5: They sittin' on snake eggs—Tryna hatch danger and poison. Crack one open, and a snake come out. Eat it? You dead.
59.6: All that mess they spun? It can't cover nothin'. Can't clothe you in righteousness. All their works are dirty, And they stay ready with violence in hand.
59.7: Their feet move fast toward evil. They quick to spill innocent blood. Their minds stay in the gutter, Leavin' destruction wherever they walk.
59.8: Peace? They don't know her. Justice? Ain't in their lane. Their paths are twisted, And anybody who follows 'em ain't gon' know peace.
59.9: That's why justice stay far from us. We try to chase righteousness, but it don't catch us. We lookin' for light, But keep walkin' in darkness.
59.10: We feelin' around like we blind, Like we got no vision at all. Stumblin' at high noon like it's midnight. We out here lookin' half-dead in these streets.
59.11: We growlin' like bears, Moanin' like doves—Lookin' for justice but not findin' it. Lookin' for a way out, but it's like salvation ghosted us.
59.12: Our sins? Yeah, they loud. They testify against us. We know what we did. Ain't even tryin' to pretend.
59.13: We turned our backs on the Lord, Lyin', schemin', Talkin' oppression and rebellion like it's cute, Pushin' out lies straight from the heart.
59.14: Justice got pushed back. Righteousness standin' off in the distance. Truth? Laid out in the street. Ain't no room for fairness.
59.15: Truth got shut down, And anybody who tries to do right becomes a target. Then the Lord looked… And He was not feelin' it. He saw the mess and said, "Ain't nobody steppin' up?"
59.16: He saw there was no one standin' in the gap—No intercessor. So He said, "Bet." I'll handle this Myself. His righteousness held Him down. His own arm brought the rescue.
59.17: He geared up: Righteousness on His chest like armor, Helmet of salvation on His head, Vengeance in His fit, Zeal wrapped around Him like a cloak.
59.18: He came with receipts. And He comin' to collect. Enemies? They gettin' what's owed. The whole earth, even the coastlines, gon' feel the payback.
59.19: Folks from the west to the east gon' respect His name. When the enemy rushes in like a flood, God's Spirit gon' raise the banner and say, "Back up!"
59.20: And guess what? The Redeemer gon' show up in Zion—For everybody in Jacob that turns away from sin.
59.21: "This right here My promise," says the Lord: "My Spirit stayin' with you. My words gon' stay in your mouth—And your kids' mouths, And your grandkids' mouths too. Forever. Bet on that."

60.1: Get up and shine, baby! Yo' light here now. God's glory? It's sittin' on you heavy.
60.2: Yeah, the world lookin' real dark, People deep in the shadows—But the Lord gon' rise over you, And His shine gon' be undeniable.
60.3: Nations gon' come follow your glow, Kings gon' pull up just to bask in your light.
60.4: Look up and take it all in: They comin'. From everywhere. Your sons comin' home, Your daughters right by your side, safe and held.
60.5: When you see it, your face gon' light up—Your heart gon' swell up with joy, 'Cause wealth from the seas and riches from all over Gon' be pourin' in.
60.6: Camels gon' flood your land—Midian, Ephah, Sheba too. They comin' with gold and incense, Puttin' praise on God's name with every step.
60.7: Kedar sendin' flocks, Nebaioth bringin' rams—All of 'em welcomed at the altar, All of it honorin' God's house.
60.8: "Who's that flyin' like clouds in the sky?" Like doves glidin' back home?
60.9: That's the coastlands waitin' on Me. Ships from Tarshish pullin' up first, Bringing your people home with silver and gold—All of it done for the name of the Lord, 'Cause He put His glory on you.
60.10: Even foreigners gon' be buildin' your walls, Their kings gon' serve you. I was mad for a minute—But now? Mercy.
60.11: Your gates? They stay open—day and night. Wealth flowin' in nonstop, Kings showin' up in long lines just to honor you.
60.12: Any nation that don't ride with you? They done. Wiped clean.
60.13: Lebanon sendin' its finest trees—Cypress, pine, and boxwood—All to deck out My sanctuary, To make My spot glow with glory.
60.14: The same folks who tried you? Yeah, they gon' bow down now. They gon' call you "The City of the Lord," Zion, where the Holy One stays.
60.15: You was once left out and looked down on, People ain't even walk through your hood. But now? You that eternal excellence. Generations gon' smile when they speak your name.
60.16: You gon' be nourished by the nations, Drink from the wealth of kings. Then you'll know—God is your Savior, Your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
60.17: God say: "I'm upgradin' everything—Gold instead of bronze, Silver instead of iron, Bronze where there was wood, Iron where there were stones. And yo' leaders? They gon' be peace and righteousness."
60.18: Violence? Gone. No more destruction in your streets. Your walls gon' be called Salvation, Your gates gon' shout Praise.
60.19: Forget the sun and moon—You don't need 'em no more. God Himself gon' be your light forever. His presence? Your glow.
60.20: No more nightfall. No more sadness. God stayin' lit in your life forever. Mourning? Over.
60.21: Everybody in your land gon' be righteous, Holdin' it down forever. God planted them, shaped them—All of it to reflect His glory.
60.22: That little one? Gon' turn into a thousand. That small one? A whole strong nation. And when God say it's time? It's happenin' quick.

61.1: The Spirit of the Lord God restin' on Me heavy, 'Cause He chose Me, anointed Me, To bring good news to the broke and hopeless, To patch up hearts that done been shattered, To let the captives know they free now, To swing open them jail doors for the ones locked down.
61.2: I came to tell y'all: This right here is the Lord's year—The year He say, "Enough's enough." And His payback? It's comin'. But for those who been cryin'? Comfort's on the way.
61.3: For the ones in Zion still in mourning, He got beauty comin' outta all that ash. He pourin' joy like oil on them sorrowful heads, Givin' folks praise instead of depression and heaviness. They gon' be called oaks of righteousness, Planted by the Lord—So folks know this His work, not theirs.
61.4: They gon' rebuild what been torn down, Raise up what generations let fall. All them hood blocks, all them ghost towns? They gon' shine again.
61.5: Strangers gon' work your fields and flocks, Outsiders tendin' to your vineyards—While you walkin' in favor.
61.6: Y'all gon' be known as God's priests, People gon' call y'all His crew. You gon' eat off the riches of the nations, And flex in the glory they used to claim.
61.7: Instead of shame? Double up. Instead of confusion? Pure joy. You gon' own double in your land, And joy that don't expire gon' be yours forever.
61.8: God say: "I love justice. I ain't here for that fake, shady worship. I'm gon' lead 'em right and lock in My covenant for eternity."
61.9: Their babies gon' be known across borders, Their descendants respected everywhere. People gon' point and say, "That right there? Yeah, God blessed them."
61.10: I can't help it—I'm rejoicin' in the Lord! My soul dancin' over here. He done dressed me in salvation, Covered me in righteousness like a fresh tailored fit. I look like a groom on wedding day, Or a bride decked out in all her glory.
61.11: Just like the earth push out flowers in spring, Just like gardens sprout what's been planted, That's how the Lord gon' make righteousness and praise bloom All over this earth, Where everybody can see.

62.1: I ain't stayin' quiet 'bout Zion. I ain't finna rest 'til she shine bright like justice, 'Til her salvation glow like a lit lamp.
62.2: The nations gon' peep your righteousness, Even kings gon' recognize your glow-up. And you? You gettin' a new name—One straight from God's own mouth.
62.3: You gon' be a crown of glory in His hand, A royal jewel God holds close.
62.4: You ain't gon' be called "Left Behind" no more, Your land won't be known as "Washed Up." Nah—your new name is Hephzibah ("My delight is in her"), And your land is Beulah ("Married"). 'Cause God got joy in you now, And He claimin' your land like a groom claims his bride.
62.5: Just like a young man puts a ring on his girl, That's how your people gon' come back to you. And the same way a groom get hype on his wedding day, That's how your God feel about you.
62.6: I got watchmen posted on the walls of Jerusalem—They don't clock out, day or night. All y'all who keep prayin'? Don't stop.
62.7: Keep remindin' God, keep pushin' til He make Jerusalem pop off And become praise on this earth.
62.8: The Lord swore—right hand raised, flexin' His strength: "You won't work hard and have it stolen anymore. No more foreigners eatin' what you sweated for."
62.9: Nah—you gon' eat the grain you gathered And praise the Lord while doin' it. You gon' sip that wine in His holy place Like royalty.
62.10: Go ahead, pass through the gates! Clear the way for the people! Build that road, raise it high, Toss the stones aside, Hold that banner up high so the world sees.
62.11: God done made the announcement—worldwide: Tell Zion's daughter: "Your salvation on the way. Look—He's bringin' His reward, And He got work lined up ahead."
62.12: They gon' call y'all The Holy People, The Ones the Lord Saved. And you? You gon' be known as Sought Out, That City That Ain't Been Left Behind.

63.1: Who that comin' up outta Edom, Rockin' that blood-red fit from Bozrah? Lookin' majestic, movin' strong, Talkin' like He got power AND righteousness? "It's Me—the one who speaks truth and saves souls."
63.2: Why your clothes look like you been stompin' grapes? Like you been in the winepress?
63.3: "I pressed that winepress all by Myself—ain't nobody helped Me. I stomped 'em out in My anger, Trampled 'em in My wrath. Blood flew up on My garments, Stained every robe I got.
63.4: Vengeance been sittin' in My heart for a minute, And now? Now it's payback time for My people.
63.5: I looked around for backup—nobody. Nobody stood up, so My own arm brought salvation. I held it down Myself.
63.6: I crushed nations, made 'em reel like drunk folks, Dropped 'em to the ground—done."
63.7: But lemme talk 'bout God's goodness now. All them blessings He gave us, All that mercy and love He showed Israel. He came through time and time again, Kept us close 'cause of His kindness.
